sections.heading: 1. Kill Imaginary Megawatts Before They Consume Option Capital
paragraphs: The first fatal trap is buying a power narrative instead of a documented service pathway. A parcel beside a 230 kV line has geographic proximity, not reserved capacity, a permissible tap, transformer availability, or an energization commitment. Screen 69kV–345kV corridors in QGIS, then attach the utility's dated response, applicable study scope, requested load shape, service voltage, and outstanding conditions to each parcel record. Label public hosting maps and ISO queue entries as screening evidence; neither establishes deliverable load. Generation interconnection procedures under 18 CFR 35.28 do not automatically establish a data center's retail service rights. Separate the utility's documented quantity from the buyer's requested quantity and from any quantity merely assumed in marketing. If a buyer discusses $4,000 per MW for a requested 100 MW campus, the tempting fee is $400,000. If utility documentation supports only a conditional 20 MW first phase, the same illustrative rate supports at most $80,000 of conditional milestone consideration, subject to the actual agreement. Unresolved upgrades or dates can reduce present assignable value further. Never sell the unsupported 80 MW as inventory; obtain additional evidence or reprice the opportunity around the smaller phase before spending another extension dollar.

The second and third traps are treating storage as ordinary load and interpreting a queue position as protection from restudies. A standalone BESS option on 5–25 acres needs separate import and export assumptions, charging restrictions, discharge duration, and interconnection cost allocation. A 50 MW, 200 MWh proposal describes four hours of nominal discharge, not 50 MW of continuously available campus supply. Ask whether charging requires a separate service arrangement and whether export limitations alter dispatch economics. Obtain the current study agreement and distinguish deposits, withdrawal exposure, security postings, and potentially refundable balances. Suppose a buyer's underwriting initially assigns $3 million of upgrades to a project, then a restudy identifies $11 million. The $8 million increase can erase the buyer's development spread without creating any additional fee for the originator. Maintain a change register keyed to study revisions, affected facilities, and cost responsibility. As an illustrative house threshold, pause discretionary parcel spending when estimated upgrades rise more than 20% or the utility withdraws the prior service schedule. Resume only after the buyer updates its economics and accepts the revised exposure in writing. If that acceptance fails, use the option's negotiated exit rather than funding a queue obligation outside the origination mandate.

The fourth trap is underwriting a campus as if it were a larger battery parcel. AI facilities can require diverse fiber entrances, carrier route verification, cooling-water capacity or a viable alternative cooling design, acoustic treatment, backup generation permissions, and staged load acceptance. Two carrier brands sharing one conduit are not physical diversity. A nearby water main is not an allocation letter. Use carrier route evidence and utility correspondence rather than broker maps to establish each critical dependency. Align a 12–24 month diligence-contingent option with realistic service milestones; a nominal 18-month option does not solve a four-year energization schedule unless extension rights and the eventual buyer's holding economics support that mismatch. Track option days remaining, termination notice deadlines, next study delivery, and estimated service date as separate fields. Flag fewer than 120 days to expiry when material utility or zoning questions remain; this is a house intervention threshold, not a statutory period. A $3,000 monthly extension for six months costs $18,000 before surveys, consultants, or legal work. Require a named buyer sponsor and a documented next evidence event before authorizing that spend. Otherwise terminate on time, preserve reusable diligence, and stop describing the parcel as powered land in outbound materials.

callout.title: Veteran Tactics for Preserving the Evidence Premium
callout.body: Sell the quality and transferability of the diligence package, not an unsupported impression of electrical abundance.
items: Maintain separate GIS layers for public screening estimates, utility-supported quantities, and executed service commitments; prevent automatic promotion between layers.
Request the assumptions behind each utility response, including coincident load, phasing, voltage, and excluded upgrades, before quoting any per-MW milestone.
Negotiate extension payments that credit against exercise consideration where obtainable, while recording the full cash burn if the option expires.
Ask each prospective BESS buyer for its import, export, duration, and upgrade ceiling before paying for parcel-specific studies that the buyer cannot use.

sections.heading: 2. Expose Title Defects, Licensing Risk, and Municipal Stop Orders
paragraphs: The fifth trap is assuming every signed option creates transferable inventory. Read assignment, change-of-control, access, exclusivity, extension, and termination provisions together. A seller's discretionary consent can make a nominally assignable interest commercially unusable; a nonrefundable extension payable before the next study arrives can create forced speculation. Obtain the owner's authority documents, title commitment, legal description, and negotiated memorandum recording rights where appropriate. Recording is not a cure for defective ownership or an unenforceable agreement. Have local counsel and the title company reconcile lien releases, existing leases, access easements, restrictive covenants, and mineral interests. A mineral waiver must cover the relevant parties and surface impacts; a seller cannot waive rights they do not own. Model a simple loss ledger: three rejected options at $5,000 each plus three $2,000 diligence packages consume $21,000 before a successful assignment. That leakage belongs in the origination portfolio, not in an abandoned spreadsheet. If assignability depends on consent, obtain the consent before promising an unconditional transfer. If the seller refuses workable language, stop paying for portable studies whose commercial benefit may accrue entirely to the seller or a competing buyer after your option expires.

The sixth trap is confusing principal dealing with brokerage immunity. Operate through a genuine owned option interest or use an appropriately licensed state broker when the activity requires one. The legal analysis follows the actual conduct, compensation, disclosures, and jurisdiction, not a spreadsheet label saying assignment fee. Texas Occupations Code Sections 1101.002 and 1101.004 illustrate why equitable-interest transactions require fact-specific review and appropriate written disclosure rather than an assumed nationwide exception. Marketing another owner's parcel for a contingent fee without the necessary authority can create licensing exposure and jeopardize collection. The seventh trap is accepting a zoning map as an operational permit. Obtain the ordinance text, current amendments, hearing calendar, use classification, and written planning response addressing the actual battery or campus design. Track moratorium proposals alongside enacted restrictions, and distinguish existing entitlements from hoped-for approvals. A parcel zoned industrial may still require special treatment for battery storage, diesel generation, height, setbacks, or noise. Stop new nonrecoverable spending when a proposed local restriction would defeat the specific use unless counsel identifies a credible path and the buyer funds that risk. Do not quietly substitute a different use in the same marketing package.

The eighth and ninth traps are trusting desktop environmental screens and dismissing emergency-access geometry. FEMA flood maps, USFWS wetland mapping, and aerial imagery identify questions; they do not establish buildable acreage or permit eligibility. Under Clean Water Act Section 404, 33 U.S.C. 1344, discharges of dredged or fill material into jurisdictional waters can require authorization. Have qualified specialists evaluate jurisdiction and project impacts rather than treating every mapped wet area as either automatically prohibited or automatically harmless. Historic industrial use also warrants environmental assessment: CERCLA liability under 42 U.S.C. 9607 and the all appropriate inquiries framework in 40 CFR Part 312 matter when structuring acquisition and evaluating available defenses. An option does not eliminate every liability created by site activities or later ownership. For BESS, verify locally adopted fire requirements, apparatus access, separation distances, drainage, and emergency response expectations with the authority having jurisdiction. NFPA 855 and UL 9540A can inform that discussion but are not universal parcel approvals. If a ten-acre site loses four acres to constraints, recalculate the equipment layout and economic capacity on six usable acres. Terminate when the revised design cannot meet the buyer's minimum capacity within its accepted cost envelope.

callout.title: Four Pre-Flight Checks Before a Nonrecoverable Payment
callout.body: These checks are internal spending controls. Each requires a dated artifact, an accountable reviewer, and a recorded decision.
items: Verify that the option binds the necessary owners and that assignment, access, extension, notice, and refund provisions match the planned transaction.
Verify that utility evidence supports the marketed quantity and conditions, with import and export treatment separated for storage projects.
Verify that current zoning, proposed restrictions, environmental constraints, and fire-access geometry leave a commercially usable project footprint.
Verify that licensing analysis, required interest disclosures, buyer funding evidence, and the maximum authorized loss are documented before payment.

sections.heading: 3. Reconcile Clawbacks, Burn, and Alternative-Use Economics
paragraphs: The tenth trap is counting an assignment headline as collected, unrestricted profit. Build a waterfall separating signed consideration, contingent milestones, cash received, escrow holdbacks, recognized revenue, direct costs, and remaining recourse. A $150,000 agreement with $90,000 payable at transfer and $60,000 payable after a service milestone is not $150,000 of immediately spendable cash. If $20,000 of the first payment remains in escrow, available cash is $70,000 before costs. Determine revenue recognition under the applicable contract and ASC 606 performance obligations and variable consideration constraints; cash timing alone does not settle recognition. A buyer may demand repayment for title defects, inaccurate study representations, missed transfer conditions, or expressly negotiated post-closing failures. Distinguish those clauses from a buyer's ordinary development risk. Negotiate clear triggers, claim periods, liability allocation, and limits appropriate to the transaction. Never describe a broad refund covenant as harmless boilerplate. As an illustrative circuit breaker, reserve the full reasonably exposed amount of a disputed payment and suspend owner distributions while the claim remains unresolved. A large bank balance can coexist with negative free cash when refund obligations, unpaid consultants, and near-term extension commitments sit outside the headline deal tracker.

Keep the canonical scenarios unchanged while testing failure sensitivity outside them. Conservative revenue of $110,000 less $77,000 of aggregate costs leaves $33,000, a 30% margin with 1 FT + 3 C. Base revenue of $505,000 less $292,900 leaves $212,100, a 42.0% margin with 1 FT + 3 C. Scaled revenue of $900,000 less $414,000 leaves $486,000, a 54% margin with 2 FT + 4 C. These revenues represent realized option assignment fees, origination milestones, and development carry, excluding underlying land purchase price, construction capex, and buyer project value. Where the operator acts as agent, assess principal-versus-agent presentation and recognize the retained operator consideration rather than routing third-party receipts into revenue. No separate retained-share factor is supplied here, so do not invent one. Explicitly allocate expired option fees within the aggregate cost budget: the illustrative $21,000 failed-site cohort must fit inside those costs unless identified as incremental stress. If incremental to Base, unchanged revenue and $313,900 costs produce $191,100 profit, approximately 37.84% margin; that is a stress test, not a replacement scorecard. Maintain a rolling thirteen-week cash forecast because the $10,000–$50,000 startup range and $1,800–$11,000 monthly opex range leave little room for uncontrolled extension chains.

The eleventh trap is treating alternative uses as free downside insurance. Apply dot_digital_billboard_and_ios_master_lease_flip only through separate, independently viable underwriting. Digital billboard options require Highway Beautification Act review under 23 U.S.C. 131, applicable state DOT spacing and digital operation rules, and local zoning permission. A battery setback does not establish a billboard entitlement. For a separate three- to ten-acre truck or equipment drop-yard IOS site, obtain explicit permitted use, assignment, and subletting rights. Illustratively, $8,000 monthly ground rent and $16,000–$22,400 monthly NNN sublease receipts produce the targeted 2.0x–2.8x ratio only if local demand supports occupancy and pricing. At the low end, annual receipts of $192,000 less $96,000 ground rent and $24,000 retained costs leave $72,000 before transaction-specific capital requirements. One vacant quarter removes $48,000 of receipts if no replacement tenant pays. A 16x–22x headline applied to $192,000 suggests $3.072–$4.224 million, but that is a gross-rent arithmetic illustration, not a supported sale price. An infrastructure REIT or other qualified buyer must evaluate actual net cash flow, transferable rights, remaining lease term, and renewal exposure. Exercise negotiated termination rights before conditions expire; avoid unfunded construction commitments and pursue only consented alternatives.

sections.heading: 4. Instrument the Pipeline and Stop Trust-Destroying Shortcuts
paragraphs: The twelfth trap is manufacturing confidence through unauthorized data access or altered evidence. Shared utility portal credentials, scraped private developer rooms, fabricated study letters, misleading ownership claims, and paid permit promises can cause account termination, contract rescission, civil claims, or criminal exposure depending on the conduct. Never bypass access restrictions or present another applicant's study as transferable capacity. Public information can still carry reuse limits, and a buyer's confidentiality agreement may restrict redistribution of route maps or commercial terms. Use authorized utility channels, permitted bulk downloads, and a controlled data room with named recipients. Record source, acquisition date, usage restrictions, document version, and the person who validated each material assertion. If a portal denies access, stop automated requests and resolve access through its published support process rather than rotating accounts. If evidence is challenged, freeze the affected claim, preserve the original artifact, and notify recipients of the correction. Maintain separate internal and buyer-facing fields so a tentative analyst estimate cannot silently become a marketing fact. The recovery path is an accurate corrected package with permission to distribute it, not a replacement identity or a more aggressive outreach sequence designed to outrun the original defect.

Build telemetry around loss mechanisms rather than dashboard decoration. Define utility-validation rate as sites receiving a documented viable next service step divided by sites completing utility screening; do not include untouched leads in the denominator. Define expired-option burn as forfeited option and extension payments divided by collected operator fees over the same trailing period, while retaining cohort views for long-cycle deals. If collected fees are zero, display the dollar burn and liquidity runway instead of manufacturing a percentage. Illustrative house thresholds include expired-option burn above 15%, a service-date slip exceeding six months, upgrade exposure beyond the buyer's written ceiling, or any missed contractual notice deadline. Each threshold must name an action: freeze new options, reprice milestones, obtain funded extensions, or terminate. Track assignment-consent completion, refund exposure by buyer, and concentration in one utility territory. A cohort of ten screened sites with two documented viable paths has a 20% validation rate; that informs sourcing quality but does not establish a universal benchmark. Review adverse changes weekly and source-system changes daily where authorized feeds support that cadence. Count stale documents as exceptions requiring review, not automatically as proof that capacity has disappeared.

Run a weekly exception meeting with the owner, transaction counsel, utility specialist, and relevant contractor; the small team does not justify blurred decision rights. Every active option needs a maximum additional loss, a next evidence event, an accountable person, and a termination date that includes delivery requirements. Reconcile option notices against executed documents rather than relying solely on a calendar import. Consider a twelve-month option with $6,000 already spent, $4,000 of pending studies, and a $3,000 extension due next week. The immediate decision concerns $7,000 of incremental exposure, not defending the sunk $6,000. If the next study cannot answer the buyer's decisive service question, declining that spend may preserve more value than another month of nominal control. For disputed assignments, reconcile the factual record with counsel before accepting or rejecting a refund demand, and preserve all relevant communications. After termination, confirm notice receipt, cancel revocable vendor orders, remove stale marketing, and document continuing confidentiality or indemnity obligations. Retain only independently viable permitted operations and buyer-consented alternative uses. The operating objective is not maximum acreage controlled; it is collectible, defensible operator consideration per dollar and hour exposed across the entire origination portfolio.

sop_steps.title: Reconcile the Evidence Ledger
sop_steps.action: Compare each marketed assertion with its current source artifact.
sop_steps.detail: Record utility quantities, conditions, study revisions, permit status, interest ownership, and authorized distribution rights; flag every unsupported assertion for immediate correction.

sop_steps.title: Calculate the Next-Dollar Exposure
sop_steps.action: Separate sunk costs from avoidable payments and binding obligations.
sop_steps.detail: Update the thirteen-week cash forecast with extensions, study invoices, potential refunds, escrow restrictions, and expired-option reserves before considering another site.

sop_steps.title: Assign the Circuit-Breaker Decision
sop_steps.action: Choose a documented continuation, repricing, funded extension, or exit.
sop_steps.detail: Name the responsible decision maker and the evidence required to reopen spending; record buyer acceptance of any revised quantity, cost, schedule, or transfer condition.

sop_steps.title: Close the Operational Loop
sop_steps.action: Deliver notices, update recipients, and verify the resulting obligations.
sop_steps.detail: Retain delivery receipts, cancel revocable orders, remove obsolete marketing, reconcile remaining liabilities, and feed the loss reason back into parcel screening.

chapters.pull_quote: An option earns its spread from transferable evidence, not from acreage beside a transmission line.
action_checklist: Create separate evidence fields for requested MW, utility-supported MW, outstanding upgrades, and realistic service dates before issuing another buyer package.
Audit every active option for owner authority, assignment consent, termination delivery requirements, extension pricing, and the maximum additional loss.
Separate 5–25 acre BESS layouts from campus models, then verify import and export pathways, usable acreage, fire access, fiber routes, and cooling dependencies as applicable.
Reconcile the canonical $33,000, $212,100, and $486,000 annual profit cases while explicitly allocating failed-option costs and tracking incremental stress separately.
Underwrite billboard and IOS alternatives independently using DOT and local permissions, actual lease rights, achievable occupancy, retained costs, and remaining term.
Activate weekly burn, restudy, deadline, refund, and evidence exceptions; stop unauthorized access and distribute traceable corrections whenever a material claim changes.

chapters.question_prompt: Where do high-margin deals, clients, or undervalued assets hide in ai data-center powered land, substation headroom & bess site optioning, and what repeatable outbound/inbound sourcing system lands the first 3-to-10 wins (2–6 months)?
chapters.title: Sourcing, Demand Mining & Landing Your First Deals
chapters.subtitle: Mine Utility Study Signals, County Records and Fiber Routes; Convert 12–24 Month Options into Documented-MW Assignments
chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #47 ranks #15 of 49 with a 92/100 Money-to-Manpower Score. Its 11 mapped plays reward evidence-led origination, not speculative claims about nearby wires. Build separate buyer mandates for standalone BESS parcels and AI data-center campuses, mine utility and county records, and obtain assignable options only after testing power, zoning, title and buyer fit. This chapter turns those signals into a measurable outbound cadence, paid milestone structure and first-deal funnel. The canonical annual owner profit cases are $33,000 Conservative, $212,100 Base and $486,000 Scaled. Recognized operator revenue consists of realized assignment fees, origination milestones and development carry; land prices and construction budgets stay outside revenue. The mapped solar-equity play receives a separate ownership, allocation and securities review.

sections.heading: 1. Mine buyer demand before paying for parcel control
paragraphs: Start with a buyer thesis, not a countywide land list. Interview ten active developers across two utility territories and record their actual acquisition filters: minimum documented MW, acceptable service date, upgrade exposure, parcel geometry, purchase ceiling, assignment structure and diligence budget. Separate standalone BESS demand for 5–25 acres from AI campuses requiring distinct fiber, water or alternative cooling, road access and zoning analysis. A developer seeking a 20 MW, 80 MWh battery is not a substitute buyer for a 60 MW computing load. Ask who signs an acquisition letter, who approves engineering expense and which investment committee date governs the search. Capture each answer in Airtable or a controlled spreadsheet with territory, evidence date, named decision maker and expiration date. Treat an unsupported expression of interest as an interview, not a mandate. A usable written mandate states the parcel type, territory, technical criteria, compensation basis and authority to act; agency work proceeds through the required licensed channel. Obtain permission before circulating a buyer's identity. Your first commercial advantage is knowing exactly which documented constraint a funded buyer will pay to remove, rather than owning a large spreadsheet of parcels nobody has requested. Refresh this demand sheet every two weeks during launch.

Build the supply feed from county assessor parcels, recorder instruments, planning agendas, utility tariffs, public capital plans and applicable ISO interconnection reports. QGIS can join parcel polygons to published 69kV–345kV substation locations, FEMA flood layers and U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service wetland mapping. Preserve source dates and coordinate systems; a mislabeled voltage or shifted polygon can waste an option deposit. Public hosting-capacity maps often describe distribution generation, not large-load service or transmission injection capability. Label those distinctions explicitly. FERC Order No. 2023 generation-interconnection reforms do not make a computing campus entitled to load service, and a queue withdrawal does not automatically release usable capacity. Mine withdrawals as a question for the utility, not a claim for the sales deck. Planning agenda items for transformer replacements, industrial rezoning and road extensions can reveal timing before marketed land prices adjust. Verify dark fiber with carrier engineering and a route-specific serviceability response; an FCC broadband map does not establish available strands or diverse entry routes. Log public-record intent triggers alongside the underlying instrument or agenda page, then assign a human reviewer before any owner contact. Respect portal access conditions and exclude restricted infrastructure information from the buyer-facing packet.

Prioritize owners whose timing problem matches your buyer's delivery window: retiring industrial operators, estate-held frontage, agricultural tracts beside established industrial districts and expired development contracts. These are hypotheses to verify, not assumptions about distress. Read recorded easements, option memoranda, mortgages and mineral reservations before promising clean control. County tax delinquency can identify a conversation but does not prove transferable title or seller motivation. Ask the owner for their preferred closing horizon and existing contractual commitments, then compare those answers with utility study timing. Pursue 12–24 month diligence-contingent options only where the seller understands extensions, assignment rights, access rights and deposit treatment. A short, expensive option on an unstudied campus is usually inventory decay, not arbitrage. Establish two sourcing queues: low-cost research candidates and capital-approved option candidates. For example, review forty parcels without deposits, advance eight to engineering calls and price only three option proposals after buyer feedback. Those counts are a launch experiment, not a historical conversion claim. The practical fallback for weak utility evidence is a permission-to-investigate arrangement or continued desktop diligence, not a higher advertised MW figure. Keep owner correspondence, parcel identifiers and all negative findings attached to the same record so a rejected parcel does not reappear as a fresh opportunity.

callout.title: Find the information gap without buying the engineering risk
callout.body: Experienced originators buy time and documentary clarity before committing meaningful option capital.
items: Ask utility representatives which published study assumptions have changed since the last map revision; record the answer, date and limits of its authority.
Request carrier route diversity by physical segment, including shared bridges and entrances; two invoices do not establish two independent paths.
Ask title counsel to search option memoranda and amendments, not merely deed ownership; a parcel can appear available while control remains encumbered.
Negotiate small initial diligence consideration with priced extensions tied to actual study progress, rather than paying the entire option budget before the utility responds.

sections.heading: 2. Score power, control and buildability before underwriting fees
paragraphs: Use a 100-point qualification scorecard with separate evidence fields: power documentation earns thirty points, upgrade-cost visibility twenty, energization schedule fifteen, title and assignability fifteen, zoning and physical buildability ten, and verified buyer fit ten. These weights are an internal prioritization policy, not a utility rating. Require seventy-five points before proposing a capital commitment, but never let arithmetic override a fatal defect. An absent legal access route, prohibited use or unsupported power claim stops advancement regardless of total score. Distinguish desktop proximity, preliminary utility response, completed study and executed service arrangements. Record requested MW separately from documented deliverable MW, including contingency assumptions and whether the document reserves anything. Where no utility document supports deliverability, leave pricing contingent on verification rather than inserting requested capacity into a valuation. Track import and export separately for BESS, including charging restrictions and operating limits. Obtain a written upgrade estimate with allocation method, estimate class, exclusions, security requirements and restudy triggers. A parcel beside a large substation can still require a long feeder, transformer procurement or upstream reinforcement. Commission qualified power engineering on shortlisted sites, and preserve the engineer's qualifications and unresolved questions in the packet. Recheck documents immediately before offering assignment terms because queue and service assumptions can change.

Model the parcel types independently. For an illustrative ten-acre BESS site, suppose utility documentation supports 20 MW import and export under stated conditions and the buyer specifies four hours of storage. The operating concept is 80 MWh, but acreage sufficiency still depends on equipment layout, fire access, setbacks and stormwater requirements. A $1,500-per-MW origination milestone would equal $30,000 only when the contract's documented-power and acceptance conditions are satisfied. It is operator fee revenue, not battery sales or electricity revenue. A separate 60 MW campus prospect requires its own service evidence, fiber serviceability, cooling assumptions, water availability where applicable and municipal use determination. Never transfer the BESS study's conclusion to the campus simply because both parcels share a station name. Compare a buyer-approved $2 million upgrade allowance with a later $5 million estimate: the $3 million increase belongs in the project's viability analysis, not quietly inside the originator's optimistic fee forecast. Pause expenditure, reprice the option or terminate under negotiated diligence rights. A 2029 service estimate also cannot satisfy a buyer requiring 2027 operation. Price control against documented deliverable MW, remaining upgrade exposure and a realistic energization path; discount unresolved conditions rather than multiplying unverified acreage by a fashionable regional price.

Underwrite option losses as a recurring sourcing cost. The canonical annual totals remain $110,000 revenue and $33,000 owner net profit at 30% margin; $505,000 and $212,100 at 42.0%; and $900,000 and $486,000 at 54%. The corresponding total expense envelopes are $77,000, $292,900 and $414,000. Within those envelopes, an illustrative failed-option reserve can be three expired deposits of $3,000, six of $4,000 and eight of $5,000 respectively: $9,000, $24,000 and $40,000. These are allocations within expenses, never extra deductions from the supplied profit figures. Maintain a rolling cash forecast because deposits and engineering invoices precede assignment collections. Starting capital of $10,000–$50,000 and monthly operating expense of $1,800–$11,000 require staged commitments; the monthly range does not by itself explain every annual project cost. Separate recurring overhead from transaction diligence, contractor expense and expired consideration. Keep the Conservative and Base teams at one full-time operator plus three contractors; Scaled uses two full-time operators plus four contractors. Engage survey, title, environmental and electrical specialists through scoped assignments rather than assuming each specialty requires permanent headcount. Stop new deposits when committed cash would breach the chosen liquidity reserve. A theoretically attractive assignment spread does not rescue an operator who cannot fund the study period.

callout.title: Four verifications before any nonrecoverable option payment
callout.body: Advance only when the file answers these questions with current documents and accountable reviewers.
items: Verify the utility document's project identity, date, supported MW, conditions and reservation status; distinguish a study result from an executed service commitment.
Verify title, legal access, assignability, extension mechanics and the local licensing treatment of the intended principal or broker role.

sections.heading: 3. Run a permission-aware cadence that converts evidence into mandates
paragraphs: Build a six-touch, twenty-one-day sequence around one verified reason to talk. On day one, send a short business email identifying the parcel class, utility territory, documented study status and one relevant buyer constraint. Ask for a fifteen-minute qualification call, not a blind confidentiality agreement. On day three, call the published business number and leave a factual callback message if appropriate. On day six, send a LinkedIn connection request without revealing confidential parcel details. On day ten, share a redacted one-page evidence brief with a source date and explicit unresolved items. On day fifteen, request an introduction through a civil engineer, broker or carrier contact who has permission to connect both parties. On day twenty-one, close the loop and ask whether the territory should remain on their acquisition watchlist. Apply 15 U.S.C. § 7704 to commercial email, including accurate headers, required identification, a valid postal address and a working opt-out honored within the statutory period. Use manual business outreach; automated calling or texting needs a separate review of 47 U.S.C. § 227 and applicable state rules. Suppress opt-outs across every campaign. Inbound pages should publish territory-specific research and a buyer criteria form, not an unsupported inventory of available powered acreage.

For launch planning, use a deliberately explicit test funnel rather than claiming industry benchmarks. Over eight weeks, research 240 account-and-territory records and qualify 120 for outreach after removing duplicates and poor fits. Target thirty substantive replies, eighteen discovery calls, nine written criteria sheets and six site-specific diligence engagements. That is 50% research qualification, 25% reply conversion, 60% reply-to-call conversion, 50% call-to-criteria conversion and approximately 67% criteria-to-engagement conversion. Seek three initial paid wins from those six engagements, a 50% engagement-to-paid conversion and 1.25% raw-record-to-paid conversion. These are operating hypotheses to revise weekly, not observed performance. Define a paid win as a collected fee for a satisfied milestone or completed assignment; an unsigned proposal, signed confidentiality agreement or unpaid mandate is not revenue. Track unique assets separately from invoices so three payments on one parcel do not become three acquired sites. If replies arrive but criteria sheets do not, tighten qualification and decision-maker access. If criteria sheets arrive but engagements stall, inspect power evidence and option economics before increasing outbound volume. Reaching ten paid wins may require repeated cohorts, a stronger conversion rate or multiple legitimate milestones; it is not implied by this single funnel. Keep the stated 2–6 month first-deal window as a planning range, with utility timing explicitly capable of extending it.

Handle objections with documents and a bounded next action. When a buyer says the parcel has no power, agree if deliverability remains unstudied and offer a utility-defined inquiry path rather than defending a map pin. When an owner rejects a long option, explain the study sequence and propose staged extensions with clear outside dates; if the required period remains unacceptable, abandon the fit. When a developer objects to an assignment fee, show the controlled rights, diligence deliverables and avoided sourcing work, then negotiate a measurable milestone instead of inventing appreciation. When procurement requests exclusivity, limit territory, duration and named assets, and require defined diligence activity before extending it. Keep a separate objection code for upgrade uncertainty, zoning conflict, schedule mismatch and missing authority so the weekly review identifies the actual bottleneck. Use a secure data room with role-limited access, document versions and a disclosure log. Give buyers enough redacted evidence to qualify interest before sharing owner identities under agreed confidentiality terms. Never imply confidentiality creates capacity rights or changes licensing requirements. The best first assignment normally comes from a narrow match between an active mandate and an honestly documented parcel, not from the largest mailing list. Ask every qualified rejection which concrete condition would make the site investable, then record the answer for future sourcing.

sop_steps.action: Interview ten developers across two selected utility territories.
sop_steps.detail: Record acquisition authority, technical criteria, upgrade tolerance, target service date and permitted compensation structure before sourcing paid options.

sections.heading: 4. Close cleanly, reconcile the scorecard and isolate the solar-equity play
paragraphs: Translate the annual scorecard into an illustrative invoice mix without changing its totals. Conservative can comprise two $40,000 assignment fees plus three $10,000 accepted origination milestones, producing $110,000. Base can comprise five $65,000 assignments plus six $30,000 milestones, producing $505,000. Scaled can comprise eight $75,000 assignments plus ten $30,000 milestones, producing $900,000. Milestones may relate to the same assets as assignments only when contracts make them distinct, payable services without duplicate consideration; credit earlier payments when the agreement requires it. These examples assume no development carry realization during the year. Do not add speculative carry value to recognized fees. Apply the supplied margins to obtain $33,000, $212,100 and $486,000 annual owner net profit, and preserve the stated staffing assumptions. The originator does not recognize the buyer's land purchase price, battery procurement, campus construction budget or project funding as operator revenue. If collecting amounts on behalf of others, assess the ASC 606 principal-versus-agent treatment and recognize only the amount earned under the applicable arrangement. This scorecard supplies no separate retained-share multiplier, so inventing one would break reconciliation. Review acceptance conditions, refund rights and performance obligations with the accountant; a cash deposit is not automatically earned revenue. Keep the operating cash forecast separate from the revenue recognition schedule.

The mandatory mapped play solar_tax_equity_depreciation_strip_syndication belongs in a separate workstream whenever a commercial solar investment genuinely complements the buyer's project. Arrange partnership-flip investments that allocate supported tax benefits and cash flows to genuine equity owners; depreciation cannot be sold as a standalone credit. For a deliberately simplified allocation example, assume an independently reviewed partnership has $100,000 of allowable depreciation in a period and supports a 70% allocation to one equity investor. That investor's allocated deduction is $70,000, not $70,000 of cash and not operator fee revenue. Actual use depends on the investor's circumstances and applicable limitations. Do not derive that percentage merely from a check size or label it a universal flip structure. Review allocations under 26 U.S.C. § 704, depreciation under § 168 and economic substance under § 7701(o) where relevant; tax basis, debt, recapture and ownership economics require transaction-specific analysis. Securities offerings also require a registration or exemption analysis under 15 U.S.C. § 77e, and transaction-based compensation can implicate broker registration under § 78o. Keep solar investor materials outside the ordinary parcel assignment deck. If ownership, allocations or intermediary authority cannot be supported, suspend solicitation and closing, use appropriately licensed intermediaries, and restructure only as independently reviewed genuine equity ownership. Never plug prospective tax benefits into the land-originator revenue model.

Close the first transactions with a documentary chain that survives a buyer's investment committee and a later accounting review. Counsel should confirm the actual option interest, assignment permissions, seller obligations, access scope and any memorandum suitable for recording. Trading as a principal does not automatically remove state licensing questions; the substance of the activity matters. Texas Occupations Code § 1101.0045 illustrates a state-specific equitable-interest disclosure framework, but its applicability to a particular option requires review rather than assumption. Use a licensed state real-estate broker where the work requires one. Deliver utility documents with their limitations intact, a current zoning determination or clearly identified unresolved status, title exceptions and a dated diligence index. Wetland screening is preliminary; discharges of dredged or fill material into covered waters may require authorization under 33 U.S.C. § 1344. Obtain the buyer's contractual acceptance and reconcile the closing statement to payment instructions verified through an established contact channel. sections.heading: 1. Originate an evidence-backed interest before pricing a megawatt
paragraphs: Start every parcel with a county parcel identifier, ownership extract, geometry checksum, seller contact authority, and separate load or generation intent. QGIS can intersect county parcel polygons with FEMA flood layers, USFWS wetland inventories, utility territory boundaries, and published 69kV–345kV infrastructure. Those intersections rank research effort; they do not establish available capacity. Query the serving utility for the proposed service configuration, requested demand, study pathway, upgrade allocation, required deposits, and energization schedule. Record the document date and its limitations alongside every MW field. A generation queue position does not reserve large-load service, and a battery charging requirement cannot be assumed satisfied by an export study. FERC interconnection requirements implemented through 18 CFR § 35.28 operate through applicable tariffs and procedures; identify the actual provider and jurisdiction before adopting a deadline. An attractive parcel remains research inventory until the utility supplies a sufficiently specific written basis for valuation. Underwrite twenty documented MW differently from twenty requested MW, even when both appear in the same developer presentation. If the utility will not bound the exposure, offer a diligence extension rather than increasing the land-option payment. Keep the unsupported capacity claim out of every buyer-facing summary.

Split the product at intake. A standalone BESS parcel commonly occupies 5–25 acres, but usable area must survive setbacks, access requirements, drainage, equipment spacing, emergency response access, and the actual interconnection design. Track charge capacity, discharge capacity, duration, and operating restrictions separately. A campus requires a different record: demand ramp, fiber route diversity, water strategy, cooling assumptions, building envelope, backup generation, and local use classification. Two fiber providers sharing one conduit do not create physical diversity. Secure carrier route evidence and utility service assumptions rather than inferring connectivity from a road crossing. For a twenty-MW campus, an illustrative $60,000 assignment equals $3,000 per documented MW; a $4 million upgrade estimate implies another $200,000 per MW of project exposure, not operator income. Test whether the buyer still accepts the site after the upgrade and schedule sensitivity. A twenty-five-MW battery assignment at $40,000 equals $1,600 per documented MW and belongs in its own comparison set. Neither multiple values land ownership, installed equipment, or speculative future power. If water or zoning fails for the campus, evaluate a separate battery concept only after confirming that its utility pathway and permitted use remain independently viable.

Control the interest with a 12–24 month diligence-contingent option whose assignment language, extension price, access rights, termination mechanics, and recording treatment fit the state and transaction. Have local counsel resolve mineral reservations, severed surface rights, lender restrictions, title exceptions, and any memorandum recording requirements before paying substantial consideration. Trade an actual principal interest or use an appropriately licensed brokerage relationship; describing a fee as an assignment does not settle the state licensing analysis. Require dated municipal confirmation of use classification and current moratorium status. A planning discussion is not an issued permit. Wetland screening also remains preliminary: potential discharge of dredged or fill material requires analysis under 33 U.S.C. § 1344, while flood development requirements depend on the applicable local program and site work. Budget failed options explicitly. Six expired interests costing $2,000 each consume $12,000 even if the two successful interests close profitably. The operating owner should authorize each irreversible payment against a dated evidence packet, a remaining research budget, and a termination calendar. Assign title, civil, and utility work to three scoped contractors instead of turning every preliminary lead into an open-ended engineering engagement.

sections.heading: 2. Install six transactional modules and make replay a harmless event
paragraphs: The six reference modules below form one deliberately bounded SQLite implementation. Save the named files together in an operator-controlled project, run ledger_core.py once, and import the remaining functions from that directory. They are reference artifacts embedded in this chapter, not imports required by this volume module. Use Python 3.9 or later and a local filesystem; do not put the database on a shared network drive. Every writer opens its own connection, enables foreign keys, and enters BEGIN IMMEDIATE before reading data that controls a write. SQLite therefore serializes competing write decisions. Busy timeouts can fail an operation without partially committing it; retry the original key and identical payload after investigating persistent contention. UNIQUE constraints protect parcel identities, event keys, journal references, and statement matches. A replay with changed content raises an error instead of silently substituting new instructions. The schema stores integer cents and balanced two-account entries, avoiding binary floating-point currency. Preserve the database, document archive, and application version together in encrypted backups, and exercise restoration before admitting real closings. Filesystem access remains restricted to the service account because database constraints do not replace control over who can open or replace the file.

Scoring is intentionally a qualification test rather than an automated valuation. The intake script requires bounded upgrade exposure, a utility reference, a positive documented MW figure, and a usable schedule before labeling a parcel screened. It checks battery acreage independently from campus fiber and water evidence. The verification module then requires current human attestations linked to document hashes; no software routine pretends that a hash proves engineering correctness. Its state progression separates screening, verification, escrow readiness, and executed closing. Terminal scrubs and expirations remain visible. Every advancing event carries an expected version, so a stale browser tab cannot overwrite a later decision. An event and its notification outbox row commit together. The dispatcher holds the write lock while submitting one notification to a receiver that must persistently honor the event key. If the receiver accepts the request and the local process crashes, the same key can be submitted again without duplicate external effect. This is a receiver contract, not a claim that SQLite alone creates distributed exactly-once delivery. Never connect that notification endpoint directly to a wire-transfer action. Escrow professionals authenticate payment instructions outside this reference, including independent callbacks for changed beneficiary details.

Journal events distinguish earning a fee from collecting it. An accepted $46,250 performance event debits receivable and credits fee revenue; a $36,250 receipt debits cash and credits receivable, leaving $10,000 outstanding. An option payment debits prepaid option and credits cash until the adopted accounting policy requires expense recognition or another treatment. The cohort illustrates expense upon expiration for the failed interests. Record owner funding against capital rather than revenue, and never post a buyer's land purchase or battery construction budget as an origination fee. The reconciliation view reports earned revenue, expense, operating profit, and cash movement separately. Statement imports match one actual cash transaction to one cash journal event; bundled net settlements require a separate clearing design before use, not invented gross bank lines. QA runs within one consistent locked snapshot and requires every recorded cash movement to have a matching statement line at period close. External statement completeness still requires opening balance, closing balance, and source-file checks. The reference prevents competing writers from winning the same transition; it does not remove utility uncertainty, document fraud, contract interpretation, or the need to review an unexpected accounting balance.

    new_version INTEGER NOT NULL,
    UNIQUE(site_id, new_version)
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS outbox (
    event_key TEXT PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES workflow_event(event_key),
    body TEXT NOT NULL,
    delivered INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK(delivered IN (0,1))
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS account (
    code TEXT PRIMARY KEY
);
INSERT OR IGNORE INTO account(code) VALUES
    ('cash'), ('receivable'), ('fee_revenue'), ('expense'),
    ('prepaid_option'), ('owner_capital');
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS journal (
    event_key TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    request_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
    booked_on TEXT NOT NULL,
    site_id TEXT REFERENCES site(site_id),
    debit_account TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES account(code),
    credit_account TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES account(code),
    amount_cents INTEGER NOT NULL
        CHECK(typeof(amount_cents) = 'integer' AND amount_cents > 0),
    CHECK(debit_account <> credit_account)
);
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS journal_no_update
BEFORE UPDATE ON journal BEGIN
    SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'Append a reversing event instead');
END;
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS journal_no_delete
BEFORE DELETE ON journal BEGIN
    SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'Retain the original journal event');
END;
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS bank_line (
    statement_key TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    journal_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE REFERENCES journal(event_key),
    amount_cents INTEGER NOT NULL
        CHECK(typeof(amount_cents) = 'integer' AND amount_cents <> 0)
);
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS bank_no_update
BEFORE UPDATE ON bank_line BEGIN
    SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'Retain the original statement match');
END;
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS bank_no_delete
BEFORE DELETE ON bank_line BEGIN
    SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'Retain the original statement match');
END;
CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS monthly_reconciliation AS
SELECT substr(booked_on, 1, 7) AS month,
    SUM(CASE WHEN credit_account = 'fee_revenue' THEN amount_cents
             WHEN debit_account = 'fee_revenue' THEN -amount_cents
             ELSE 0 END) AS revenue_cents,
    SUM(CASE WHEN debit_account = 'expense' THEN amount_cents
             WHEN credit_account = 'expense' THEN -amount_cents
             ELSE 0 END) AS expense_cents,
    SUM(CASE WHEN debit_account = 'cash' THEN amount_cents
             WHEN credit_account = 'cash' THEN -amount_cents
             ELSE 0 END) AS cash_delta_cents
FROM journal GROUP BY substr(booked_on, 1, 7);
CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS account_balance AS
SELECT a.code,
    COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN j.debit_account = a.code THEN j.amount_cents
                      WHEN j.credit_account = a.code THEN -j.amount_cents
                      ELSE 0 END), 0) AS debit_balance_cents
FROM account a LEFT JOIN journal j
    ON a.code = j.debit_account OR a.code = j.credit_account
GROUP BY a.code;
"""

def fingerprint(value):
    raw = json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':'))
    return hashlib.sha256(raw.encode('utf-8')).hexdigest()

def connect(path='ledger.sqlite3'):
    con = sqlite3.connect(path, timeout=60, isolation_level=None)
    con.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    con.execute('PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON')
    con.execute('PRAGMA busy_timeout = 60000')
    con.execute('PRAGMA synchronous = FULL')
    return con

@contextmanager
def atomic(con):
    con.execute('BEGIN IMMEDIATE')
    try:
        yield
        con.execute('COMMIT')
    except BaseException:
        if con.in_transaction:
            con.execute('ROLLBACK')
        raise

def initialize(path='ledger.sqlite3'):
    con = connect(path)
    try:
        con.executescript(SCHEMA)
    finally:
        con.close()

if __name__ == '__main__':
    initialize()

from __future__ import annotations
from datetime import date
from ledger_core import atomic, fingerprint

def post(con, event_key, booked_on, debit, credit, cents, site_id=None):
    if type(cents) is not int or cents <= 0:
        raise ValueError('Journal amounts require positive integer cents')
    parsed = date.fromisoformat(booked_on)
    if parsed.isoformat() != booked_on:
        raise ValueError('Use a canonical ISO calendar date')
    request = [booked_on, site_id, debit, credit, cents]
    digest = fingerprint(request)
    with atomic(con):
        prior = con.execute(
            'SELECT request_hash FROM journal WHERE event_key=?', (event_key,)
        ).fetchone()
        if prior:
            if prior['request_hash'] != digest:
                raise ValueError('Journal key was reused with changed content')
            return event_key
        con.execute(
            'INSERT INTO journal VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,?)',
            (event_key, digest, booked_on, site_id, debit, credit, cents)
        )
        return event_key

sections.heading: 3. Walk ninety days from thirty first-month leads to reconciled Base cash
paragraphs: The Worked 90-Day Cohort Walk uses three monthly intake cohorts and two completed assignments from the first cohort. It is an illustrative operating schedule, not a prediction that every new business closes within ninety days. The stated two-to-six-month first-deal range still applies. Begin with $50,000 owner capital, the upper end of the $10,000–$50,000 startup range. Month 1 admits thirty research leads: eighteen fail the desktop screen, twelve receive deeper diligence, and seven of those twelve eventually fail utility or zoning work. Four failures are utility-related and three are zoning-related. Three surviving prospects are parked without further paid commitments; two advance to closing. Six failed interests each consume $2,000 of option consideration, while one additional failed prospect is rejected before payment. Month 2 admits twenty-four new leads, rejects sixteen, and leaves eight in evidence collection. Month 3 admits twenty-four, rejects eighteen, and leaves six awaiting deeper qualification. These later prospects produce no revenue or additional paid option exposure inside the window. Across seventy-eight leads, fifty-nine are scrubbed, three are parked, two close, and fourteen remain active. The count reconciliation prevents a presentation from silently recycling failed parcels as fresh qualified inventory.

Site A is a ten-acre BESS interest with twenty-five MW supported by the relevant utility documentation and its stated conditions. Month 2 earns a $40,000 assignment and realizes $6,250 of contracted development carry. The latter is settled consideration, not an appraisal of future upside. Of the $46,250 earned, $36,250 arrives during Month 2 and $10,000 remains receivable. Site B is an eighty-acre campus interest supporting a documented twenty-MW service plan with separately accepted upgrade and schedule exposure. Month 3 earns its $60,000 assignment plus four distinct $5,000 origination milestones. Those four milestones are expressly priced deliverables: accepted utility package, accepted title package, accepted carrier evidence, and completed option assignment package. They are not four additional sites or invented capacity awards. Month 3 collects all $80,000 plus Site A's $10,000 receivable. Total earned revenue and collected receipts both reach $126,250. The reference assumes the contract and accounting assessment support recognition at these acceptance events; an enforceability or performance dispute delays recognition rather than creating a balancing entry. Neither site is described as already energized, and the buyer packet preserves every utility qualification that informed the assignment price.

Expense recognition and cash payment differ until the prepaid-option balance unwinds. Month 1 pays $6,000 of failed-option consideration, expenses $2,000 on expiration, and carries $4,000 forward. Month 2 pays another $6,000, expenses the earlier $4,000, and carries $6,000. Month 3 expenses that remaining $6,000 without another payment. Other costs are paid when incurred. Recurring overhead is $6,000, $7,500, and $9,000 respectively, within the stated monthly range; transaction-specific contractor work and failed-option charges sit outside that recurring overhead line. Total expenses are $18,225, $25,000, and $30,000. Consequently cash outflows are $22,225, $27,000, and $24,000. Ending cash moves from the initial $50,000 to $27,775, $37,025, and $103,025. No owner distribution is assumed. Quarter profit and incremental operating cash both equal $53,025 because receivables and prepaid options finish at zero. Multiplying the quarter by four produces $505,000 revenue, $292,900 expense, and $212,100 owner profit, exactly 42.0%. That is a normalized Base run rate, not a claim that the fourteen remaining leads guarantee three identical future quarters. Recurring capital remains in cash and is never counted again as operating income.

sections.heading: 4. Map eleven operating plays without importing credit inventory risk
paragraphs: The eleven mapped plays here are chapter-local workflow mappings, not eleven claimed catalog identifiers. The first ten are parcel intake, electrical screening, utility validation, BESS separation, campus infrastructure, title diligence, zoning diligence, option structuring, developer placement, and cash reconciliation. The eleventh uses the supplied catalog identifier transferable_tax_credit_brokerage_syndication. Keep the first ten connected through the site identifier: electrical evidence changes valuation, title evidence changes assignability, and contract acceptance changes revenue timing. This prevents an attractive tax-credit discussion from bypassing a weak land interest. At the illustrated Base pace, eight annual assignments generate $400,000, sixteen accepted milestones generate $80,000, and realized carry generates $25,000. Those components total $505,000 without adding land price, installed battery value, or a speculative credit spread. The same owner and three contractors support the Base team assumption through bounded work orders and reusable evidence packets. Scale to two full-time people and four contractors only when transaction throughput supports the stated $900,000 revenue case. A longer queue or a municipal moratorium requires pausing commitments, not hiring ahead of unverified volume. Track expense per rejected prospect and per closed interest so automation savings remain observable rather than assumed.

For transferable_tax_credit_brokerage_syndication, originate potential introductions from actual ISO, RTO, and utility queue publications, developer announcements, DOE project resources, EPA program records, state film offices, and historic-preservation registries. DOE and EPA are not a universal interconnection-queue authority; their records supply research leads, not proof of credit eligibility or ownership. IRC § 6418 covers specified eligible federal credits, with cash consideration, unrelated-party, election, registration, and other requirements addressed by the statute and Treasury regulations. Federal rehabilitation credit under IRC § 47 is not automatically included merely because a historic project appears in a registry. Georgia film credits, Louisiana film incentives, and state historic or brownfield programs require separate analysis of the particular state's certification, transfer, redemption, and taxpayer-use rules. Do not treat them as interchangeable federal instruments. For an eligible $1 million credit transaction, seller proceeds at $0.85 and buyer payment at $0.94 imply $850,000 and $940,000 respectively, leaving a $90,000 gross economic spread before insurance, escrow, specialists, and other costs. That arithmetic is an illustrative adjacent transaction, not additional Base revenue, and it does not authorize the operator to buy and resell a federal credit as inventory.

Structure the federal example as a direct eligible-taxpayer transfer to the ultimate buyer, coordinated through a simultaneous buyer-funded escrow with separately documented operator compensation. Section 6418 generally prevents a transferee from transferring the same credit again, so a literal intermediary resale is the wrong structure. For a state program, establish whether successive transfers are permitted before designing any back-to-back legs. Across the supplied $0.82–$0.88 seller range and $0.92–$0.96 buyer range, a $1 million face amount implies a $40,000–$140,000 gross pricing difference, not automatic retained income. Assess principal-versus-agent presentation under ASC 606 and recognize only the compensation the operator actually earns under the applicable conclusion. No retained-share percentage is supplied for this volume, so none is invented. Never fund unhedged credit inventory from the land-option budget. Require simultaneous escrow funded by the buyer's wire and the specified non-cancelable tax-credit insurance protection before pursuing this mapped play. Inspect exclusions, recapture treatment, beneficiaries, insurer conditions, and premium funding; insurance does not correct an ineligible transfer. If the required coverage or direct-transfer structure cannot be obtained, decline the credit execution and continue the independently viable land-option work. The Base ledger remains complete without this adjacent spread.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #47, ranked #15 of 49 with a 92/100 Money-to-Manpower Score, turns fragmented parcel, power, environmental, and title evidence into assignable development options. Across 11 mapped plays, the information advantage comes from reconciling authoritative records, not collecting more map pins. This chapter specifies an eighteen-source directory, a reproducible enrichment waterfall, mineral-election safeguards, and evidence standards for developer handoff. Separate standalone BESS parcels from AI campuses, and price only utility-documented deliverable MW with explicit upgrade exposure and energization assumptions. The canonical annual owner-profit cases are $33,000 Conservative, $212,100 Base, and $486,000 Scaled. Those outcomes derive from realized assignment and origination revenue, excluding land purchase prices and project capital expenditure; expired-option losses remain operating costs.

sections.heading: 1. Establish the parcel, power, and ownership evidence hierarchy
paragraphs: Start with a parcel evidence register, not a statewide heat map. Give each candidate a county identifier, assessor parcel number, normalized geometry, recorded owner, instrument reference, source date, retrieval date, and permitted-use note. Keep assessor ownership separate from recorder evidence because tax rolls can lag conveyances and frequently omit mineral reservations, access limitations, or option-related instruments. Query the county assessor's GIS REST service where published; otherwise download its released parcel file or request the current extract. Retrieve deeds, easements, plats, and relevant memoranda through the recorder's index, then order title work before paying meaningful option consideration. Regrid accelerates cross-county discovery but does not replace the county record or a title commitment. Deduplicate by county plus parcel identifier, preserving split and merger history rather than joining on an address alone. An illustrative screen of 1,000 parcels might yield 100 accessible sites and 20 title-review candidates; those are workflow counts, not conversion promises. Track each rejection reason so the next acquisition batch excludes the same access defect. A cheap parcel beside expensive infrastructure is still a poor option when the seller cannot convey the required surface rights or authorize a transferable diligence package.

Build the power layer from three distinct evidence classes: physical infrastructure, published interconnection activity, and site-specific utility correspondence. HIFLD transmission geometry can help identify 69kV–345kV corridors, while ISO queue exports show proposed generation or storage projects and their published status. Neither establishes spare import capacity for an AI campus. A distribution hosting-capacity map also cannot substitute for a transmission-connected large-load study. Record load import, BESS charging import, and BESS export separately; a project may require different studies, tariffs, and operating restrictions for each direction. Request a dated utility response identifying the contemplated point of connection, deliverable MW assumptions, required studies, upgrade responsibility, and earliest credible service sequence. Store whether the response is preliminary, conditional, or backed by an executed agreement. FERC eLibrary helps trace tariff proceedings and relevant filings, but critical energy infrastructure information is restricted under 18 CFR 388.113. Use public material and authorized customer channels rather than attempting to reconstruct restricted network detail. If the utility cannot substantiate capacity, retain the parcel as an unvalidated lead with zero power-backed valuation uplift. Physical proximity earns a question for an engineer, never a marketable capacity claim.

Use the directory's first six entries as the authoritative backbone and record source-specific limitations alongside every download. Public access commonly costs nothing, but county image fees, certified copies, commercial licenses, and specialist review still consume the acquisition budget. Distinguish publisher refresh latency from desk polling cadence: a nightly download cannot make an annually maintained parcel layer current. Configure conditional HTTP requests when supported, identify the client where requested, honor Retry-After, and cap concurrency to the published service terms. Where no numerical request limit is published, start with serial requests and a conservative delay rather than inventing an allowance. Save the source URL, response status, content hash, publication timestamp, and transformation version. For JavaScript portals without a documented export, prefer their download function or a records request over brittle automated browsing. A failed refresh must mark the dataset stale without deleting the last verified snapshot. Escalate changes in ownership, connection status, and queue withdrawal to a human because those events can invalidate a signed option package. The desk's advantage is an auditable chain from a sales statement to its underlying record, including the date and scope of the evidence.

callout.body: Spend automation on finding contradictions before spending option money on defending a favorite parcel.

sections.heading: 2. Screen buildable land before purchasing commercial enrichment
paragraphs: Run the environmental waterfall before buying contact enrichment or commissioning a developer-facing valuation. Intersect the parcel with FEMA's National Flood Hazard Layer, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service National Wetlands Inventory, NRCS soils, USGS elevation, and local zoning. Preserve each intersection as an observation, not a permitting conclusion. FEMA layers have geographic and publication gaps; absence from the downloadable layer does not establish negligible flood exposure. Wetlands Inventory polygons are screening evidence rather than a jurisdictional determination under Clean Water Act section 404, 33 U.S.C. 1344. A qualified field delineation and applicable agency process resolve the development question. Estimate contiguous buildable acreage after setbacks, access, drainage, slopes, and known constraints, avoiding double subtraction where exclusion polygons overlap. For an illustrative 20-acre BESS parcel with six acres of overlapping exclusions and two additional acres reserved for access and stormwater, begin layout work on 12 acres, not 20. Do not convert that acreage directly into MW without equipment spacing, fire access, noise, and utility design inputs. Escalate ambiguous boundaries to a surveyor or environmental specialist before representing the parcel as construction-ready to any potential assignee.

Separate standalone BESS screening from AI-campus screening at the schema level. A 5–25 acre BESS option may depend primarily on electrical configuration, fire access, setbacks, drainage, and dispatch economics; a campus also needs a credible cooling strategy, water or alternative cooling resources, fiber routes, large-load service, and a zoning pathway that accommodates its specific use. The FCC National Broadband Map describes reported availability and supporting datasets, not verified dark-fiber strands or physically diverse enterprise routes. Use it only to identify providers for follow-up. Obtain written carrier responses identifying proposed lateral construction, capacity, route diversity, splice location assumptions, and installation lead times. Two carriers occupying the same conduit do not create resilient connectivity. For water-dependent designs, request written service and allocation assumptions from the water utility; a nearby main is not an entitlement. Read municipal agendas, adopted ordinances, and pending amendments because data-center and battery moratoriums can appear between GIS updates. A planning employee's informal email is useful context but does not override an adopted ordinance. Record the proposed use description, hearing sequence, and written interpretation needed for the actual parcel rather than importing a neighboring jurisdiction's development assumptions.

The second directory segment covers six environmental, zoning, and connectivity sources. Use free bulk datasets first, then pay for targeted verification only when a parcel survives the initial screen. An illustrative batch budget could allocate $300 for document retrieval, $1,200 for preliminary environmental review, and $1,500 for power-engineering triage across ten shortlisted sites: $3,000 total, or $300 per site before option consideration. Those allocations are planning assumptions, not vendor quotations. If only two sites survive, the effective screening cost is $1,500 per survivor, which belongs in the acquisition economics rather than disappearing into software overhead. Obtain scopes and quotes for fieldwork because wetlands delineation, geotechnical work, and full utility studies are separate commitments. Keep public-data processing local where practical and upload confidential option documents to external services only with authorization and appropriate contractual controls. Map tools should display evidence age and confidence instead of a single misleading suitability score. The useful output is a ranked work queue identifying the next decisive question, the responsible specialist, the cost to answer it, and the date beyond which the answer no longer protects the option holder.

sections.heading: 3. Turn docket changes and enrichment into reproducible operator decisions
paragraphs: Implement the waterfall as append-only raw acquisition, normalized records, spatial screening, specialist verification, and publication. Python's urllib.request, csv, json, hashlib, sqlite3, and datetime support downloads, hashes, tabular transformations, storage, and UTC timestamps without importing project-specific modules. Use QGIS for spatial inspection and processing; do not pretend the standard library supplies a complete geospatial intersection engine. Keep original coordinates and declared reference systems, then calculate acreage and distance in an appropriate projected system rather than geographic degrees. Diagnose malformed geometry, duplicate parcel keys, missing source dates, changed column names, and unexpectedly empty extracts before updating the operator dashboard. Reconcile row counts and bounding boxes against the previous snapshot; quarantine suspicious changes for review. Record source URL, license, retrieval time, payload hash, parser version, and reviewer disposition in SQLite. An identical hash can skip redundant downstream work, but a new hash should not automatically invalidate every parcel. Compare relevant attributes and geometries to generate specific alerts. Keep seller contact details in an access-controlled table and avoid distributing personal records inside general developer exports. A reproducible pipeline tells the reviewer exactly which changed fact moved a parcel from viable to suspended.

The mandatory mapped play forced_pooling_mineral_lease_curve_jumping uses public pooling applications and drilling schedules to surface unleased mineral interests before applicable election deadlines. For an Oklahoma example, review Corporation Commission oil-and-gas case records, hearing materials, signed orders, and Oklahoma Statutes title 52, section 87.1; do not transplant its procedures to another state. The controlling order and applicable service rules determine the actual election sequence, not a generic calendar scraped from a hearing notice. Link legal descriptions to recorder instruments, confirm the interest through mineral title work, and ask counsel to explain permitted elections and non-consent cost exposure before acquisition. Illustratively, five net mineral acres within a 640-acre unit at a 20% royalty yield a decimal of 0.0015625. Applied to an assumed $8,000,000 royalty valuation base, that equals $12,500 before applicable deductions, taxes, title adjustments, and timing effects. It is neither a production forecast nor powered-land desk revenue. Acreage allocation can differ for multiunit development. If title, notice, or election economics remain unresolved, stop acquisitions pending counsel review and choose only timely, fully understood permitted elections. Surface-option value and speculative mineral upside stay in separate ledgers.

Enrichment should resolve a specific uncertainty at the cheapest reliable level. Begin with county instruments and Secretary of State entity records, use a licensed aggregator only to accelerate discovery, and confirm signing authority through seller-provided organizational documents. A registered agent is a service contact, not proof of beneficial ownership or authority to assign an option. For mineral screening, use public commission orders before a commercial well-history subscription; for fiber, use carrier engineering after provider discovery rather than purchasing broad contact lists. The eighteen named directory entries deliberately combine registries, downloadable feeds, authenticated APIs, and verification tools because no single endpoint resolves the investment decision. Maintain an alert queue for pooling-order issuance, material queue changes, zoning amendments, expiring seller authorizations, and option notice deadlines. Polling frequency should follow event importance and source rules: review a live election matter each business day, while unchanged elevation tiles need no daily retrieval. If a portal is unavailable, record the outage and use the official clerk or agency contact; never infer that silence means no new order. Preserve the fallback response in the same evidence register so manual diligence remains auditable.
