sections.heading: 4. Price evidence-backed options and reconcile the desk's economics
paragraphs: Price an assignable option from utility-documented deliverable MW, network-upgrade exposure, energization timing, and the rights actually controlled. Keep requested capacity, studied capacity, contracted service, and energized service in different fields. A preliminary utility letter supports only its stated assumptions; it does not create an unconditional delivery obligation. Consider an illustrative BESS option with ten utility-documented MW subject to identified conditions and a proposed $15,000-per-MW assignment fee: the conditional fee basis is $150,000. If the buyer also faces $2,000,000 of upgrades and a 36-month service sequence, those burdens affect willingness to pay and closing conditions even though they are not operator revenue. If restudy reduces usable capacity to six MW, the same fee convention yields $90,000 before any further commercial renegotiation. Model a 12–24 month diligence-contingent land option against that longer utility timeline, with express extension rights or a termination plan. Assignment language must address seller permission where required, study-transfer restrictions, diligence access, deposits, and milestone evidence. An option that expires before the decisive study arrives should not be priced as though its holder controls the eventual project. Route state-specific principal-versus-broker questions through qualified counsel.

Reconcile every dashboard to the supplied Formula v2.0 scorecard before discussing automation returns. Conservative revenue is $110,000 with $77,000 total costs, leaving $33,000 owner profit and a 30% margin. Base revenue is $505,000 with $292,900 costs, leaving $212,100 and 42.0%. Scaled revenue is $900,000 with $414,000 costs, leaving $486,000 and 54%. Teams remain 1 FT + 3 C, 1 FT + 3 C, and 2 FT + 4 C respectively. An illustrative revenue bridge uses two $40,000 assignments plus three $10,000 milestones for Conservative; five $65,000 assignments plus six $30,000 milestones for Base; and six $100,000 assignments plus six $50,000 milestones for Scaled. Count milestones only when earned, without double counting amounts credited against assignment fees. These bridges explain arithmetic rather than prescribe a closing forecast. Land purchase consideration, project capex, utility deposits paid for the developer, and mineral royalty projections are excluded. Apply ASC 606 principal-agent analysis to actual contracts; gross merchant or project cash movements are not automatically desk revenue. No separate retained_share haircut is specified for this candidate, so do not silently apply one to its canonical revenue figures.

Make failure costs visible inside the scenario totals. An illustrative Base allocation of eight expired options at $2,500 each produces $20,000 of sunk consideration already included within the $292,900 cost envelope, leaving $272,900 for every other cost. Do not subtract that burn twice, and do not erase it when showing successful-deal margins. Budget software, contractors, travel, title work, study support, and failed diligence against the same envelope; the stated $1,800–$11,000 monthly operating range does not replace total annual scenario costs. With $10,000–$50,000 startup capital and a 2–6 month first-deal target, sequence option deposits after the cheapest decisive checks and maintain cash for termination notices and specialist responses. The final operator matrix assigns measurable release conditions to a buyer packet. Obtain written authority for seller documents, verify whether option interests or memoranda should be recorded under applicable state practice, and trade as a principal or work with licensed brokers where the activity requires licensure. An evidence-backed rejection is a productive output: it preserves capital for a site whose power, title, zoning, and transfer mechanics can survive the buyer's independent diligence.

callout.title: Verify four conditions before releasing a priced assignment package
callout.body: A complete packet distinguishes controlled rights, conditional evidence, and future work without blurring their economic value.
items: Power verification: obtain dated utility evidence distinguishing import and export MW, study status, upgrade responsibility, and realistic energization timing.

chapters.pull_quote: A map locates the opportunity; documented rights, deliverable power, and survivable deadlines make it assignable.

Build a dated mineral-election calendar from controlling orders and counsel-reviewed rules; stop acquisitions whenever title or non-consent exposure remains unresolved.

Reconcile $110,000, $505,000, and $900,000 revenue cases to their exact profits, with expired-option fees inside costs and underlying project expenditures excluded.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #47, AI Data-Center Powered Land, Substation Headroom & BESS Site Optioning, ranks #15 of 49 with a 92/100 Money-to-Manpower Score and 11 mapped plays. This chapter turns that opportunity into an executable rights-and-evidence system: acquire an enforceable principal interest, establish the applicable state licensing boundary, verify utility study status, and sell precisely defined rights rather than imagined power. Annual owner profit is $33,000 Conservative, $212,100 Base, and $486,000 Scaled. The public_record_api_intelligence play supplies traceable owner and permitting signals; contracts allocate study costs, expired option fees, assignment permissions, and milestone risk. Separate BESS parcels from data-center campuses, preserve source provenance, and use outreach that states ownership, compensation, and capacity limitations accurately.

sections.heading: 1. Establish the principal interest before selling the opportunity
paragraphs: Start every parcel file with a role memorandum identifying the acquiring entity, the interest it actually holds, the property jurisdiction, and the services it will perform for anyone else. An executed option can create enforceable contract rights and, depending on state law and drafting, an equitable interest; a GIS pin, unsigned letter, or introduction does not. Recording a permitted memorandum may protect notice priority, but recording alone neither creates valid ownership nor supplies a brokerage exemption. Texas Occupations Code Section 1101.0045 expressly addresses selling an option or assigning a purchase-contract interest without brokerage activity, subject to written disclosure of the interest's nature. California Business and Professions Code Sections 10130, 10131, and 10133 require a separate analysis of compensated acts for another and applicable exemptions. Do not generalize either state's treatment nationwide. If the actual service is locating buyers, negotiating another owner's land sale, or earning compensation for procuring a counterparty, engage a properly licensed state broker under a written allocation of duties. A principal label on an invoice does not repair brokerage conduct. Keep acquisition compensation, assignment proceeds, brokerage commissions, and technical consulting fees in separate contract schedules so the facts remain auditable.

Build a jurisdiction sheet before spending the first option dollar. Record state licensing statutes, commercial versus residential scope, transaction frequency restrictions where relevant, required assignment disclosures, local land-use authority, and the professionals authorized to perform engineering or legal work. New York Real Property Law Sections 440 and 440-a define brokerage activity and impose licensing requirements; determine how the actual entity and services fit rather than importing a Texas conclusion. State wholesaling reforms sometimes target residential property specifically, so verify covered property types before applying registration or disclosure rules to a utility-scale commercial tract. Local zoning can independently prohibit a BESS use or impose a data-center moratorium even when the assignment structure is sound. Confirm signatory authority for LLC owners, trustees, estate representatives, and co-owners through documents acceptable to the closing title company. A probate docket is a diligence signal, not proof that a beneficiary can grant an option. Have state counsel resolve ambiguous authority or exemption questions before buyer solicitation. The licensed surveyor establishes boundaries, the engineer evaluates technical constraints, and the title company reports insurability exceptions; none of those functions should be implied by an automated parcel score. Preserve the dated conclusion and its supporting documents.

Use public_record_api_intelligence to detect commercial triggers, not to manufacture ownership certainty. County recorder indexes, assessor exports, probate registries, planning dockets, utility commission filings, and official APIs can expose fragmented ownership, expiring permits, industrial reuse, or new infrastructure proceedings. Unclaimed-property ledgers may help resolve entity identity where lawful access permits, but they do not establish parcel title or authorize recovery services. Federal FOIA, 5 U.S.C. Section 552, governs federal agency records; county records generally require the applicable state public-records process instead. Store source URL, retrieval date, document identifier, reuse terms, and confidence level beside each claim. An illustrative monthly batch of 300 parcels at $0.40 retrieval cost plus 12 analyst hours at $50 costs $720. If 24 survive document screening, the intelligence cost is $30 per surviving parcel, before title, engineering, or option payments. Do not count those survivors as contracted sites. When an endpoint closes or access terms prohibit automation, switch to scheduled bulk FOIA/public-record exports, official data feeds, and low-frequency cached queues. Respect rate limits and access restrictions; collect only necessary contact details. Route disputed ownership, protected personal records, and conflicting parcel identifiers to manual review rather than auto-generating seller demands.

callout.title: Make the rights file more valuable than the parcel list
callout.body: Experienced originators sell an organized, transferable evidence package. These tactics reduce preventable option burn without overstating utility readiness.
items: Ask the title company which option memorandum language and release instrument it will accept before recording anything; attach the agreed forms.
Maintain separate fields for parcel owner, authorized signer, option holder, utility applicant, and prospective assignee; these roles often differ.
Negotiate seller authorization for utility inquiries at option signing so a confidentiality objection does not consume the first diligence month.
Cache dated county exports and retain document hashes; a changed assessor name should trigger verification, not silently replace the contracting owner.

sections.heading: 2. Tie every power claim to a dated utility and permitting record
paragraphs: Treat a 69kV–345kV substation layer as a screening instrument, not a deliverability certificate. Maintain separate fields for requested MW, studied MW, conditionally available MW, contracted service, and actual energization. Each entry needs the utility or transmission provider, document date, service configuration, dependencies, expiration, and authorized disclosure scope. A hosting-capacity map may address distributed generation rather than a large load, and an ISO generation queue does not reserve data-center load service. FERC Order No. 2023 and implementing tariff changes concern generator interconnection processes within their jurisdiction; they do not replace utility retail service rules, state commission requirements, or applicable large-load procedures. For BESS, separately establish charging load, export rights, operating limitations, and whether the project follows distribution or transmission interconnection rules. For a campus, determine redundancy, ramp schedule, curtailment exposure, power quality, and construction lead times. Request written treatment of network upgrades, cost allocation, security postings, restudy events, and transfer permissions. A study number is evidence of process status only. Marketing must reproduce material conditions instead of turning a preliminary estimate into a firm delivery date. If the utility will not support the proposed MW, price the parcel as speculative land rights rather than powered inventory.

Separate a standalone BESS parcel of 5–25 acres from a data-center campus at the first screening step. The BESS file needs usable acreage after setbacks, emergency access, equipment separation, drainage, noise controls, fire-water arrangements where required, and charging/export feasibility. The campus file additionally needs dark-fiber route evidence, carrier availability, cooling design, water supply and discharge permissions, backup-generation permitting, and expansion geometry. A carrier map does not establish a service commitment or diverse physical entrances. Local adoption of NFPA 855 or fire-code provisions determines enforceable installation requirements; UL 9540 and UL 9540A documentation serve different equipment and test functions and do not themselves grant a land-use permit. Check the enacted ordinance and current moratorium language with the planning authority. Clean Water Act Section 404, 33 U.S.C. Section 1344, can require authorization for discharges of dredged or fill material into covered waters, including jurisdictional wetlands. A GIS wetland layer is not a jurisdictional determination. CERCLA liability under 42 U.S.C. Section 9607 makes environmental history material to eventual acquisition; timely all-appropriate-inquiries work and other statutory conditions matter to available protections. Require qualified investigation rather than assuming a clean-looking agricultural parcel has no environmental exposure.

Value the option against utility-documented deliverable MW, upgrade exposure, and a credible energization schedule, then discount for remaining conditions. Illustratively, a milestone priced at $2,500 per qualifying MW produces $50,000 only when 20 MW satisfy the contract's evidence definition. If an authorized utility update supports just 12 qualifying MW, the same formula produces $30,000; if the evidence threshold is unmet, that milestone produces zero. These are underwriting mechanics, not additional scorecard revenue. A $4 million upgrade estimate on 20 MW equals $200,000 per MW of developer capital exposure, not originator revenue. Set a buyer-specific upgrade ceiling and latest acceptable energization date, and give the option holder a termination or repricing mechanism when either fails. Budget failed sites explicitly: four expired options at $3,000 each consume $12,000 before recovered deposits or transferable reports. Keep that burn inside the scenario expense envelope rather than subtracting it again from canonical profit. Underwrite BESS revenue and operating assumptions separately from campus economics; an attractive battery location may fail data-center fiber or water requirements. Do not capitalize hoped-for development carry as current fees. A dated utility correction should immediately update valuation, buyer materials, and the decision on the next extension payment.

callout.title: Four checks before releasing a buyer-facing package
callout.body: Release only the claims supported by the current file. A failed check changes the package, the price, or the decision to proceed.
items: Verify the option remains effective, the seller had signing authority, and assignment and diligence-sharing permissions cover the proposed buyer.
Verify every MW and energization statement against a dated utility document, including restudy exposure, conditions, and disclosure restrictions.
Verify current zoning and moratorium status for the actual use, with BESS and campus requirements tracked in separate diligence paths.
Verify the jurisdictional licensing position, buyer compensation disclosures, expired-option reserve, and written authority for each external contact.

sections.heading: 3. Draft transferable rights and reconcile every fee to the scorecard
paragraphs: Use a 12–24 month diligence-contingent option only when its extension economics match the likely utility and entitlement calendar. Identify the legal description, purchase-price mechanism, option consideration, payment recipient, effective date, exercise procedure, notice addresses, and exact expiration time. Separate the initial term from paid extensions and state which payments are refundable, credited at closing, or earned immediately. Do not bury a utility-dependent business plan inside an unconditional payment schedule. Give the holder defined access for surveys, environmental investigation, utility meetings, and carrier inquiries, subject to insurance, restoration, and restrictions on invasive work. Address easements, mineral and surface-use conflicts, access rights, title objections, and seller cooperation with applications. Assignment language must distinguish land-option rights from utility applications, study agreements, permits, and consultant reports, each of which may require separate consent or reapplication. Specify notice-only transfers, permitted affiliates, third-party consent standards, and whether the original holder remains liable. Attach any recordable memorandum and the release obligation after termination. An option that cannot be transferred on the buyer's schedule is not assignment inventory merely because its cover page says assignable. Calendar exercise notices with redundant reminders and delivery evidence; missing an exact contractual deadline can destroy an otherwise valuable position without any deterioration in the site.

Define fee triggers so an accountant and a hostile counterparty reach the same answer. An assignment fee should identify the transferred interest, closing conditions, escrow instructions, and payment timing. A per-MW milestone needs the qualifying utility evidence, measurement unit, partial-performance treatment, dispute procedure, and exclusion of previously paid quantities. Development carry needs a distribution waterfall, reporting rights, dilution treatment, and realization conditions; unsigned projections are not earned fees. The canonical Conservative case is $110,000 revenue less $77,000 expenses, producing $33,000 at 30%. Base is $505,000 less $292,900, producing $212,100 at 42.0%. Scaled is $900,000 less $414,000, producing $486,000 at 54%. Illustrative fee compositions are two $55,000 assignments; five $85,000 assignments plus four separate $20,000 milestones; and six $100,000 assignments plus ten separate $30,000 milestones, respectively. Do not count a milestone twice if it is credited against an assignment fee. These compositions reconcile the scorecard rather than establish closing forecasts. Underlying land prices, loan principal, developer capex, and reimbursed third-party amounts do not become operator fee revenue merely by crossing an account. Have the accountant determine applicable recognition, asset-sale, variable-consideration, and principal-versus-agent treatment; do not invent a retained-share adjustment absent from these canonical scenarios.

Make scope, confidentiality, anti-circumvention, liability, dispute resolution, and data rights operational rather than decorative. Scope should list deliverables and exclusions, including whether utility coordination means transmitting documents or performing licensed engineering. An anti-circumvention clause should identify introduced counterparties and parcels, preserve documented pre-existing relationships, specify a reasonable survival period, and tie any remedy to enforceable terms instead of claiming ownership of every regional developer. Use a jurisdiction-appropriate liability cap with negotiated exclusions for matters such as fraud, intentional misconduct, confidentiality breaches, or unpaid amounts; enforceability and insurability require review. Allocate indemnities to actual control over access work, third-party claims, and inaccurate representations. Choose governing law, forum or arbitration procedure, notice method, interim-relief treatment, and responsibility for fees. Separate public source material from proprietary scoring logic, licensed GIS layers, seller confidential material, and commissioned reports. A paid consultant report may require an assignment or reliance letter before a buyer can use it. Grant only the data rights actually held and prohibit redistribution where source terms require it. Finally, define correction duties: a capacity reduction, title defect, or enacted moratorium must reach active counterparties promptly. Confidentiality cannot become an excuse to preserve a materially outdated sales statement.

sections.heading: 4. Run truthful outreach, structured discovery, and documented handoff
paragraphs: Segment outreach by channel and recipient before drafting the first message. CAN-SPAM, 15 U.S.C. Section 7704, applies to commercial email including business-to-business messages; use accurate routing information, a nondeceptive subject, required advertising identification where applicable, a valid physical postal address, and a working opt-out mechanism. Honor opt-outs within ten business days and maintain suppression across contractors rather than buying the same address back through another list. For calls and texts, evaluate 47 U.S.C. Section 227, 47 CFR Section 64.1200, federal do-not-call requirements where applicable, and relevant state calling and recording laws. Manual dialing is not a universal exemption from solicitation restrictions, and a business contact's published mobile number is not blanket permission for automated marketing. Determine whether the technology, destination, message purpose, and consent satisfy applicable rules before launch. Start with individually researched business email and permitted manual calls, not a high-volume text campaign. FTC Act Section 5 and state deceptive-practices laws make misleading capacity or ownership claims dangerous regardless of the channel. Maintain a campaign record containing the source, permitted purpose, message version, send date, opt-out status, and any promised follow-up. Restrict access to contact exports and remove unnecessary personal details.

Use scripts that match the actual stage of ownership, and read them verbatim only when their factual statements are true. Before acquisition, say: 'I acquire commercial site options as a principal. I am evaluating whether your parcel could support a battery facility or a data-center use. I do not represent the utility, and I have not established power availability. Would you consider a paid, time-limited option with defined diligence and assignment terms?' After execution, a buyer opening can say: 'Our entity holds an option on this parcel. We are offering our contractual interest, not representing that we own the land outright. The diligence package separates utility-confirmed facts from unresolved conditions. May I send the rights summary and evidence index?' For utility intake, say: 'We hold written owner authorization to investigate this parcel. Please identify the applicable process for the proposed load or storage configuration, required deposits, study scope, and any restrictions on sharing or transferring the resulting documents.' If authorization is absent, obtain it before using that script. These openings avoid artificial scarcity and do not turn a nearby substation into a capacity promise. Follow each conversation with a written summary identifying assumptions, requested documents, and the next decision date.

Discovery should expose disqualifiers before an extension payment comes due. Ask the developer: 'What initial and ultimate load, export capability, redundancy, curtailment tolerance, maximum upgrade contribution, and latest energization date would make this site usable?' Then ask: 'Which utility documents and transfer permissions must be present before your team pays an assignment fee or a per-MW milestone?' For a campus, add: 'What fiber diversity, cooling-water strategy, backup-generation envelope, and expansion acreage are essential?' For BESS, ask: 'What charge and discharge limits, fire-access geometry, and operating restrictions would defeat your design?' Record answers as acceptance criteria, not loose sales notes. When evidence changes, use a correction script: 'The utility's latest written position changes the capacity assumption in our earlier package. Please stop using that version. We will provide the replacement evidence and revised commercial terms before requesting any commitment.' A decline closes with: 'Understood. We will record your preference and stop further marketing contact through this channel.' The handoff package should contain the signed rights chain, evidence index, unresolved issues, cost responsibility schedule, approved message history, and milestone ledger. Require a named person to own each unresolved item. Automation can prepare reminders and comparison reports, but it cannot convert missing authority or unsupported MW into a sellable fact.

sections.heading: 1. Build an evidence pipeline before increasing parcel throughput
paragraphs: Start with a parcel-centered evidence ledger, not a chatbot searching for cheap land. A Python scheduler retrieves permitted downloads from PJM, MISO, ERCOT, utility hosting-capacity portals, county GIS services, and recorder indexes. Use urllib.request for transport, csv and json for structured records, sqlite3 for the local ledger, and hashlib for immutable source fingerprints. Each observation carries the source URL, retrieval time, effective date, coordinate reference, parser version, and parcel identifier. Queue identifiers belong in a separate relationship table because one project can span several parcels and one parcel can attract several proposals. Keep raw snapshots alongside normalized fields so a changed column name cannot silently alter a capacity claim. Public availability does not establish permission for unlimited automated access; honor access terms, request limits, and licensed reuse boundaries. Schedule county ownership refreshes separately from utility engineering updates. A daily deed event may justify owner outreach, while a monthly utility map cannot support a same-day capacity assertion. The eleven-play map below uses one supplied canonical identifier and ten descriptive implementation labels. Its purpose is to assign an economic test and a recovery path to every repetitive activity before volume increases.

Measure the seventy-percent objective against observed human minutes, not the percentage of screens that contain an AI feature. An illustrative benchmark processes 100 routine parcel packets with a 1,000-minute manual baseline: 420 research minutes, 240 qualification minutes, 180 fulfillment minutes, and 160 acquisition-administration minutes. After including review and exception handling, target net reductions of 330, 180, 120, and 100 minutes respectively. That removes 730 minutes, or 73%, leaving 270 human minutes. Deep utility studies, negotiations, field visits, and title resolution remain outside this routine-task benchmark and retain separate time budgets. The principal owns utility representations, option commitments, and buyer negotiations. Three contractors cover GIS and research, electrical feasibility, and title/document operations; any licensed legal work uses appropriately qualified counsel. Record reviewer identity and elapsed time at each consequential transition. If source deterioration increases review time, report the lower achieved automation rate instead of hiding those minutes in another category. Run a weekly matched sample against manual processing, checking missed restrictions and incorrect parcel joins. A faster pipeline that distributes the wrong owner or transformer evidence has increased liability and rework rather than productive capacity.

Treat language models as constrained extraction workers. Submit a bounded document excerpt and request fields such as study date, stated project type, MW quantity, limiting condition, and supporting quotation. Validate the returned JSON against explicit keys, numeric ranges, and required evidence spans before storing it. Absence of a supported value produces a pending-evidence state, never a fabricated engineering answer. Models must not obey instructions embedded in filings, contact landowners, edit option terms, or publish packets. An illustrative 100-parcel routine batch budgets $6 for licensed source access, $4 for compute, $8 for model usage, and $2 for evidence storage: $20 total, or $0.20 per parcel. The model allowance assumes two million input tokens at $2 per million and half a million output tokens at $8 per million; these are budgeting assumptions rather than vendor quotes. Adding 270 review minutes at $60 per hour produces $290, or $2.90 per routine packet. This excludes mail, surveys, engineering, legal work, and option deposits. Cap spending per batch, cache unchanged documents by fingerprint, and reroute malformed responses to deterministic parsing or manual entry rather than repeatedly paying for an unsupported answer.

sections.heading: 2. Separate map-based screening from utility-backed site qualification
paragraphs: Build two independent qualification schemas. Standalone BESS starts with a 5–25 acre parcel envelope, usable area, access geometry, fire access, setbacks, topography, charging import, discharge export, and interconnection position. An AI data-center campus adds materially different requirements: firm load service, energization phases, redundant service architecture, fiber diversity, cooling strategy, water availability where required, noise limits, and expansion area. A 69kV–345kV line near either property is only a screening feature. A hosting-capacity layer can also describe a particular generation assumption rather than firm load availability. Never translate its displayed number directly into sellable campus MW. Store service type, study scope, issuing utility, conditions, expected in-service date, and estimated network-upgrade exposure together. FERC interconnection requirements under 18 CFR 35.28 provide relevant context for covered generation interconnections; they do not replace the utility's retail load-service process or establish jurisdiction over every project. When a developer requests a capacity headline, respond with the actual documented service position and its limitations. Until the utility resolves deliverability, price the parcel as a conditional development lead rather than a powered asset. This distinction belongs in database fields, marketing text, and the assignment agreement.

Use environmental and title automation to prioritize specialist work, not to issue definitive clearance. FEMA's National Flood Hazard Layer and the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service National Wetlands Inventory can expose obvious conflicts quickly, but map age, scale, and unmapped features limit conclusions. A wetland inventory is not a jurisdictional determination under Clean Water Act Section 404, 33 U.S.C. 1344. Record source dates and route potential aquatic-resource impacts to an environmental specialist before committing to grading assumptions. County zoning portals require similar discipline: store adopted text, district boundaries, use definitions, effective dates, and temporary moratorium actions separately. A staff email may explain process without establishing an entitlement. Title extraction must flag severed mineral interests, surface-use rights, leases, easements, and missing referenced instruments. Do not describe a mineral waiver as secured until the correct rights holder has executed an effective instrument. Python can reconcile document references and flag exceptions; it cannot resolve competing property rights. For campus candidates, obtain carrier evidence covering actual serviceability and route separation. Two providers sharing the same duct bank do not create physical diversity, and a nearby backbone does not establish a usable local connection.

Value option interests against documented service outcomes and explicit downside branches. Consider an illustrative BESS candidate whose utility study supports a conditional 20 MW export position and identifies $1.2 million of upgrade exposure. At an assumed $6,000 per documented MW, a negotiated origination milestone would be $120,000; the developer's $60,000 per MW upgrade burden is separate project expenditure, not operator revenue. If a restudy doubles upgrades to $2.4 million, recalculate buyer demand and milestone probability before paying an extension. An illustrative branch with a 40% chance of collecting $120,000, $22,000 of remaining diligence and option spending, and $8,000 of closing expense only on success produces $22,800 of expected incremental contribution: $48,000 less $22,000 less $3,200. That estimate supports a decision, not booked revenue. For a campus, build a separate load-service schedule; a BESS export study cannot substitute for campus import rights. If energization slips beyond the 12–24 month option term, obtain a priced extension or terminate before the next deposit. Carry expired option fees as real portfolio expenses. A failed utility validation should reduce the budget immediately rather than survive as an optimistic pipeline asset.

sections.heading: 3. Assemble transferable option packets and reconcile every scenario
paragraphs: Turn the option packager into a controlled document compiler. Approved fields include legal owner names, parcel schedules, consideration, diligence periods, access permissions, assignment conditions, extension prices, notice methods, and termination mechanics. The model may propose an extraction from a source document, but only reviewed values enter the executable template. A milestone-contingent 12–24 month option should make utility investigation and land-use diligence commercially usable without implying that every deposit is refundable. Counsel must draft the actual conditions and notice requirements. Hold the principal's own recorded or equitable option interest where appropriate, and involve licensed state real-estate brokers when the activity requires licensure. Principal status is not a universal exemption for arranging other parties' transactions. For example, Texas Occupations Code Section 1101.002 defines covered brokerage activity; apply the full local framework to the actual compensation and conduct. The generated packet includes an evidence index, dated utility qualifications, an upgrade sensitivity, an unresolved-issues register, and a buyer-specific summary. Send a draft for principal and counsel review before signature. Capture execution and delivery evidence separately from template generation so a successful API response cannot masquerade as an effective agreement.

Reconcile the packager's commercial ledger to the canonical Formula v2.0 scorecard without importing project asset values. Conservative revenue is $110,000, expenses are $77,000, and owner net profit is $33,000 at 30%. Base revenue is $505,000, expenses are $292,900, and owner net profit is $212,100 at 42.0%. Scaled revenue is $900,000, expenses are $414,000, and owner net profit is $486,000 at 54%. Conservative and Base use 1 FT plus 3 C; Scaled uses 2 FT plus 4 C. One illustrative Base revenue composition is three $100,000 assignments, five distinct $31,000 earned milestones, and $50,000 of realized development carry. The total is exactly $505,000. Underlying land consideration, battery equipment purchases, campus construction expenditure, and developer upgrade payments never enter this revenue total merely because the operator helped originate them. Track milestone offsets so a closing payment does not count an earlier credited fee twice. Apply ASC 606 principal-versus-agent analysis to the actual contracts; third-party collections are not automatically gross operator revenue. No separate retained-share multiplier is supplied for this candidate, so do not invent one. Expected carry remains outside realized case revenue.

Make automation savings visible inside the expense envelope rather than adding them a second time to profit. An illustrative Base allocation assigns $108,000 to recurring operations, $96,000 to deal-specific contractor work, $55,000 to studies, legal work, and travel, $18,000 to expired option fees, and $15,900 to outbound acquisition. These mutually exclusive buckets total $292,900. Assign each invoice once; recurring operations and contractor work must not duplicate the same labor. The $108,000 recurring bucket equals $9,000 monthly, inside the stated $1,800–$11,000 monthly operating range, while deal expenses remain additional and lumpy. Startup capital of $10,000–$50,000 and a two-to-six-month first-deal window do not imply that every portfolio can fund its options without further receipts. Use a rolling thirteen-week cash schedule that shows deposit deadlines, review costs, expected receipts, and missed milestone branches. For the $18,000 expiry allocation, six failed options at $3,000 each provide a concrete burn assumption. If observed failures exceed it, reduce new commitments or revise the forecast while preserving the canonical reference case. Staffing expansion should follow evidenced reviewer capacity and signed demand, not a larger count of unqualified map pins.

sections.heading: 4. Compound qualified distribution without automating misleading claims
paragraphs: Implement public_filing_trigger_mail_arbitrage as a privately branded research-to-contact loop, not an imitation government demand. Where access and reuse are permitted, ingest daily Secretary of State new-LLC filings and county recorder deed or mortgage events. Resolve entity names against actual parcel ownership, suppress duplicates, and distinguish registered-agent addresses from useful operating contacts. New ownership near a screened infrastructure corridor can trigger a truthful invitation to discuss a conditional site option. The broader play also supports genuine recurring workplace compliance updates, property-tax appeal contingency offers, or permissioned exclusive new-mover and B2B introductions through appropriately qualified providers. These are separate service funnels, not extra revenue silently added to the powered-land scorecard. Prohibit government-lookalike poster or deed invoices, official-looking seals, invented citation numbers, and language suggesting mandatory payment. 39 U.S.C. 3001 restricts specified deceptive mailed solicitations; California Business and Professions Code Section 17537.9 imposes specific requirements on covered recorded-document solicitations. Review the actual offer and target state before mailing. A direct-mail API may render and dispatch an approved creative, but a human must authorize the recipient segment and final proof. If ownership resolution is weak, stop the mailing rather than multiplying bad matches with personalization.

Use explicit acquisition arithmetic to decide which distribution loop deserves another dollar. An illustrative mailing sends 200 letters at $1.10 each, costing $220, with an additional $80 of matching and review labor. At a 4% response rate, eight responses cost $37.50 each; if two become qualified owner conversations, acquisition cost is $150 per qualified conversation. A conversation is neither an option nor a closed assignment. For a separate subscription test, ten customers paying $240 annually create $2,400 of annual gross billings before provider shares, fulfillment, refunds, and acquisition costs. An appeal provider charging 20% of an actual $10,000 assessment-related tax saving earns $2,000 under that illustrative agreement, subject to the applicable practice and fee rules. Keep both experiments outside the canonical land-option forecast. For the core business, publish reviewed territory briefs with dated utility context, aggregate constraints, and an invitation to submit buyer mandates. Avoid parcel-level disclosures without permission. Track qualified introductions from each brief and ask satisfied buyers for introductions to adjacent project teams. Compensated referrals require state-specific review of brokerage restrictions. Commercial email must satisfy applicable 15 U.S.C. 7704 requirements, including accurate headers, identification, postal address, and a working opt-out process.

Keep the distribution flywheel recoverable. Incoming webhooks require signature verification, timestamp checks, replay protection, and a persisted event identifier before processing. Use hmac.compare_digest for signature comparison and a SQLite uniqueness constraint for idempotency. Separate receipt of an event from permission to send mail, release documents, or spend deposits. A retry should resume the approved action, not create another letter or duplicate invoice. Back off after rate-limit responses, quarantine malformed payloads, and retain a manual export path for source outages. If a utility revises its study, invalidate every downstream packet that references the old fingerprint and notify recipients who received affected claims. If a model fails extraction tests, switch to deterministic fields and human review without changing the evidence standard. During an outage, continue only work supported by current records; pause stale capacity claims and time-sensitive commitments. A weekly dashboard should show accepted introductions, utility validation rate, deposit burn, review minutes, packet corrections, and collected operator fees. Measure source-to-qualified-option conversion by cohort rather than celebrating raw traffic. Increase distribution only when current evidence, reviewer capacity, and cash runway support the added workload. The compounding asset is a trusted record of precise introductions, not an ever-larger address list.

chapters.question_prompt: How do you structure a lean 1 FT + 3 C (4 people) -> 2 FT + 4 C (6 people) pod, enforce weekly scorecards, and build transferable books that command a premium exit multiple (or durable cash cow)?
chapters.title: Pod Architecture, Contractor KPIs & Exit Valuation
chapters.subtitle: Four-to-Six-Person Powered-Land Pods, Utility-Evidenced MW, Accrual Cohorts, Written IP Transfers & Buyer-Normalized Earnings
chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #47, ranked #15 of 49 with a 92/100 Money-to-Manpower Score, turns powered-land and BESS origination into an evidence business rather than a parcel-listing business. This chapter organizes its 11 mapped plays into a four-person pod, then adds only two seats when accepted workload justifies six people. Contractors earn against reproducible deliverables; weekly scorecards measure utility evidence, option survival, buyer concentration, and collected contribution. Canonical annual owner profits are $33,000 Conservative, $212,100 Base, and $486,000 Scaled. Separate standalone BESS parcels from AI campuses, expense failed diligence consistently, and transfer signed rights alongside the operating records. Illustrative exit multiples apply to normalized earnings, never land purchase prices, speculative megawatts, or unsupported pipeline values.

sections.heading: 1. Assign eleven plays to four accountable seats before adding headcount
paragraphs: Build the initial pod around one full-time principal and three contractors, with one named owner for every accepted artifact. For operating purposes, map the volume's eleven plays to P01 parcel sourcing, P02 substation screening, P03 utility deliverability validation, P04 fiber and water verification, P05 zoning diligence, P06 environmental screening, P07 title and mineral diligence, P08 option structuring, P09 developer matching, P10 milestone collection, and P11 assignment and development-carry administration. These are execution labels, not eleven independent departments. The principal owns capital allocation, landowner negotiations, utility communications, buyer relationships, and collection. A GIS contractor owns reproducible spatial screening; an electrical engineer owns technical interpretation and study coordination; transaction counsel owns title exceptions, option language, assignment mechanics, and closing records. Counsel must have the relevant state authority and transaction experience. The principal remains responsible for commercial judgments that cannot be outsourced to a map or document template. Use Airtable for site records, QGIS with GeoPackage exports for spatial evidence, and a permissioned document repository for executed instruments. Every parcel receives a permanent site identifier connecting its option, utility correspondence, invoices, and buyer activity. This keeps eleven plays inside four seats without hiding work in the founder's inbox.

Buy contractor capacity as bounded deliverables rather than unlimited availability. A Base planning envelope might allocate $1,200 monthly to GIS production, $1,800 to electrical review, and $1,200 to transaction counsel, leaving $1,800 of a $6,000 core monthly budget for systems, insurance, administration, and other recurring needs. These are illustrative purchasing budgets, not quoted market rates or entitlement to unlimited professional hours. Set included hours and parcel counts in each statement of work; authorize additional studies against an identified site budget. Require GIS delivery within two business days after complete inputs, engineering triage within three, and contract redlines within five. Utility response time remains outside those contractor clocks. Accept work only when another person can reproduce the finding from linked source material. Require correction of contractor-caused defects within two business days, with exclusions for changed utility facts and new title exceptions. Pay retainers for accepted capacity, fixed fees for accepted packages, and any lawful success compensation only against collected receipts. Do not pay engineers per favorable MW conclusion. Apply actual worker classification rules, including the common-law employee test under 26 U.S.C. section 3121(d)(2), rather than assuming an invoice makes a worker independent.

Add the second employee only when a trailing twelve-week record shows recurring coordination work exceeding twenty principal hours weekly and accepted projects fund the fully loaded seat under a downside collection schedule. That employee owns records, deadline control, billing support, and independent acceptance checks, not unlicensed engineering or brokerage. Add the fourth contractor as a land-use and environmental specialist when those investigations repeatedly delay viable projects; the Scaled pod then contains exactly two employees and four contractors. Keep specialist fieldwork inside separately approved project purchases rather than pretending the standing pod can perform every survey or wetland delineation. Before work begins, obtain confidentiality terms, permitted-use rules for utility materials, and a signed assignment of transferable contractor copyright under 17 U.S.C. section 204(a). Identify pre-existing templates and third-party GIS layers separately, with licenses that support the intended business transfer. Store source files, not merely flattened reports. Separate principal option trading from compensated services for others; Texas Occupations Code sections 1101.002 and 1101.351 illustrate why activity and state law determine broker licensing exposure. Escalate the actual structure to qualified local counsel, and use licensed brokerage where required. A principal label alone does not settle that analysis or make every assignment freely transferable.

callout.title: Make technical work portable before the first assignment
callout.body: Buy evidence that survives staff turnover, utility restudies, and buyer diligence rather than presentations that depend on the original author.
items: Require the electrical reviewer to separate load-service evidence from BESS import and export permissions; one study rarely establishes all three.
Export each QGIS package with source dates, coordinate reference system, parcel identifiers, and reproducible layer joins before accepting the invoice.
Make extension notices, mineral exceptions, and assignment-consent deadlines searchable fields linked to the executed option, not notes buried in email.
Obtain transferable rights to original contractor work while preserving third-party license restrictions; a broad IP clause cannot transfer rights the contractor never owned.

sections.heading: 2. Enforce weekly evidence scorecards and reject speculative megawatts
paragraphs: Run a forty-five-minute weekly operating meeting from a frozen Monday export, not a refreshed dashboard whose history disappears. Measure each play through accepted outputs, median elapsed days, first-pass acceptance, open exceptions, and cash at risk. For P01, count parcels meeting the written buyer mandate rather than every parcel scraped. For P02, record voltage class, substation identifier, source date, and whether published hosting information actually covers the requested service. Screening 69kV–345kV infrastructure creates a research lead, not a capacity asset. For P03, require utility-originated documentation identifying the project, requested service, study stage, assumptions, and unresolved facilities before describing MW as utility-supported. Distinguish preliminary indications from executed service arrangements and record confidence separately from quantity. A queue position does not establish deliverability, and a nearby transmission line does not prove an available connection. Review changes in upgrade exposure and energization dates weekly, even when the headline MW number remains unchanged. Score contractors on accurate negative findings as well as viable sites. Otherwise, a production bonus encourages optimistic classifications, and the principal pays option fees to preserve parcels that should already have been rejected.

Maintain separate underwriting lanes for standalone BESS parcels of 5–25 acres and AI data-center campuses. BESS screening must distinguish charging demand, export capability, equipment layout, fire access, setbacks, and the applicable interconnection process. AI campuses require utility load-service evidence plus carrier-confirmed routes, credible route diversity, water and wastewater arrangements where needed, and an executable zoning path. A carrier map is not a construction commitment; two fiber products can share one physical conduit. Apply 18 CFR section 35.28 where the relevant transmission-provider tariff and interconnection framework govern, while separately checking state utility service rules and the actual utility tariff for large load. Screen flood and wetland exposure early, then commission appropriate field investigation before relying on developable acreage. Clean Water Act section 404, 33 U.S.C. section 1344, addresses discharges of dredged or fill material into jurisdictional waters; a desktop polygon cannot decide every jurisdictional question. Price each option against utility-documented deliverable MW, upgrade exposure, and realistic energization timing. Stress delayed service beyond the 12–24 month option term, including extension cost, study security, and cash consumed before assignment. Close the file when downside contribution turns negative without a funded, documented cure.

Use concentration limits as acquisition constraints rather than decorative dashboard targets. Cap each buyer group at 25% of rolling twelve-month recognized operator revenue, 25% of receivables, and 25% of probability-weighted expected fee receipts, tested separately. Aggregate affiliates and common control so five purchasing entities do not masquerade as five independent buyers. Apply the same 25% ceiling to option capital exposed to one landowner group. During startup, one closing can mechanically exceed the revenue limit; report that breach explicitly and freeze additional discretionary exposure to that group until diversification restores the limit. Do not invent alternate denominators to make the dashboard green. Also report utility-territory and municipality exposure because a restudy or zoning moratorium can impair otherwise unrelated sites. Assign each exception a responsible person, cash consequence, remedy, and date. Track first-pass package acceptance with a target of at least 95%, but audit a sample against original documents so superficial completeness cannot inflate the score. Keep observed results separate from planning targets. The meeting ends with funded next actions, rejected sites, collection owners, and an updated thirteen-week cash forecast reflecting every committed extension and study payment.

callout.title: Four pre-flight checks before committing another option dollar
callout.body: The principal records these checks against the current site version before signing, extending, or releasing a buyer package.
items: Verify utility evidence identifies the correct parcel or project, service type, MW assumptions, upgrade exposure, study stage, and credible energization dependencies.
Verify the correct BESS or AI-campus lane includes current zoning, access, title, environmental constraints, and required fiber or water service evidence.
Verify assignment rights, consent provisions, notice deadlines, extension funding, and any required licensed brokerage participation against executed documents.
Verify downside cash remains funded, expired-fee reserves remain intact, and buyer, receivable, pipeline, and landowner concentrations satisfy the stated 25% limits.

sections.heading: 3. Reconcile accrual cohorts to the canonical owner-profit cases
paragraphs: Keep three linked records: an accrual general ledger, a site-level cohort ledger, and a thirteen-week cash forecast. The general ledger controls recognized revenue and expenses; the cohort ledger explains which parcels consumed capital and produced contribution; the cash forecast controls survival between closings. Tag every entry by permanent site identifier, origination quarter, BESS or campus lane, buyer group, and cost category. Recognize assignment fees and origination milestones when the applicable contractual performance obligations are satisfied under the selected accounting policy, not merely when a promising buyer appears. Evaluate variable consideration and development carry separately; projected developer profits are not current operator revenue. Apply ASC 606 principal-versus-agent analysis where relevant, recording only the retained consideration when the operator acts as agent. The canonical scorecard here already measures operator fee revenue, so do not multiply it by an invented retained-share factor. Land purchase prices, battery capex, utility construction budgets, and campus enterprise values remain outside that revenue basis. Maintain a written policy for option cost capitalization, impairment, abandonment, and release on assignment, reviewed by the reporting accountant. An expired option cannot stay booked as a healthy asset simply because management still likes the neighboring substation.

Reconcile all three cases before discussing hiring or valuation. Conservative revenue of $110,000 less $77,000 of total modeled costs leaves $33,000, a 30% margin. Base revenue of $505,000 less $292,900 leaves $212,100, a 42.0% margin. Scaled revenue of $900,000 less $414,000 leaves $486,000, a 54% margin. The first two cases use one employee and three contractors; Scaled uses two employees and four contractors. One illustrative cost allocation assigns Conservative spending to $21,600 core operations, $9,000 expired options, $18,000 successful option basis, $18,400 project studies and title work, and $10,000 variable closing compensation. Base assigns $72,000, $24,000, $80,000, $64,900, and $52,000 respectively. Scaled assigns $132,000, $36,000, $100,000, $86,000, and $60,000 respectively. Each allocation exactly matches its total cost envelope; these categories illustrate deployment rather than replace the canonical scorecard. Core monthly operations therefore equal $1,800, $6,000, and $11,000, while project expenditures remain separately visible. Do not interpret monthly overhead as total business spending. Conservative contractor scopes must be substantially narrower than the Base purchasing envelope, and project cash timing must fit available capital before any commitment becomes binding.

Use cohort reporting to prevent attractive closed deals from concealing the unsuccessful parcels that made them possible. The Base expired-option provision of $24,000 could represent six failed sites costing $4,000 each; that is an illustrative reserve construction, not a prediction of six failures. Allocate each loss to its actual vintage and failure cause, distinguishing utility rejection, upgrade escalation, zoning restriction, title defect, and commercial abandonment. Report gross fees, successful option basis, failed option expense, external diligence, variable compensation, and allocated core operations for every closed cohort. Preserve unallocated overhead transparently instead of shifting it into future projects. A hypothetical $100,000 earned assignment fee with $40,000 collected creates $60,000 of receivables; it does not create $100,000 of available cash. Conversely, an advance subject to unsatisfied obligations generally requires liability analysis rather than immediate revenue recognition. Reconcile bank balances, escrow statements, contract assets, receivables, and option schedules monthly. The principal signs the close in the four-person pod; the operations employee prepares it after scaling, with independent accounting review purchased as needed. Keep owner distributions separate from operating expenses and identify actual owner labor when presenting normalized earnings to a buyer.

sections.heading: 4. Sell transferable earnings, or retain a documented cash-producing portfolio
paragraphs: Start exit preparation by deciding what a buyer would actually acquire: assignable options, enforceable fee contracts, transferable intellectual property, documented relationships, operating records, and a team capable of continuing production. None automatically transfers with a shared folder. Review assignment, change-of-control, confidentiality, and utility-data restrictions contract by contract. Record required consents, permitted disclosures, and retained obligations before granting diligence access. Assemble a buyer room containing monthly accrual statements, bank reconciliations, tax filings, cohort performance, option schedules, study status, concentration reports, contractor agreements, and signed IP transfers. Redact information that cannot yet be disclosed and use staged access consistent with contractual restrictions. Include failed sites and adverse utility updates; a sanitized portfolio collapses under quality-of-earnings review. Demonstrate founder independence with documented handoffs and a trial operating period during which the operations lead runs deadlines and reporting without undocumented founder intervention. Separate continuing origination earnings from one-time portfolio liquidation proceeds. A buyer may value an existing option inventory using project-specific downside analysis while valuing the repeatable sourcing operation on normalized earnings. Do not count the same expected assignment receipts once in operating earnings and again as an added portfolio asset without an explicit valuation bridge.

Use multiples as negotiation scenarios rather than asserted market comparables. For a small, founder-led, transaction-dependent operation, an illustrative 1.5–3.0 times normalized seller discretionary earnings range is a reasonable sensitivity to test, not evidence of an available offer. If diligence establishes that Base owner profit of $212,100 equals normalized discretionary earnings, that range implies $318,150–$636,300 before deal-specific cash, debt, working-capital, and portfolio adjustments. A managed business with repeatable collections, transferable relationships, and low concentration might instead be tested at 3.0–5.0 times normalized EBITDA, but the earnings base must include replacement management. Illustratively subtracting $100,000 of fully loaded replacement cost from Base owner profit leaves $112,100 only if all other EBITDA bridge adjustments net to zero. The resulting sensitivity is $336,300–$560,500. These alternative methods are not additive. Verify owner compensation, payroll burden, interest, taxes, depreciation, amortization, and genuinely nonrecurring items before choosing either measure. Recurring failed-option costs and ordinary contractor fees are not discretionary add-backs. A higher multiple applied to a properly reduced earnings base can produce less value than the founder expects, especially when collections depend on personal introductions or one unusually profitable closing.

Negotiate proceeds through a transparent bridge from operating value to seller cash, including debt-like liabilities, excess cash, normalized working capital, escrow, transaction expenses, and contingent consideration. Keep an earnout tied to clearly defined collected operator fees rather than developer capex or claimed MW. Specify treatment of restudies, buyer cancellations, delayed energization, affiliate transactions, and post-close spending decisions that could change earnout results. A premium case requires evidence of repeatable cohorts and transferable rights, not simply a large unstudied pipeline. If sale terms discount the business more heavily than its risk-adjusted cash generation warrants, retain it as a managed distribution business. Maintain option-expiry reserves, study commitments, tax reserves, and working capital before distributing cash; canonical owner profit is not automatically the amount safely withdrawable each month. Keep the same 25% concentration limits and quarterly transferability audit even without a planned sale. Test whether the four-person pod can continue Conservative or Base production during a principal absence, and whether the six-person pod genuinely reduces founder dependence at Scaled volume. The durable asset is a documented process that rejects weak sites early, prices surviving options honestly, and converts earned fees into collectible cash without concealed obligations.

chapters.pull_quote: A transferable powered-land business owns documented rights and repeatable collections, not impressive maps of power it cannot deliver.
action_checklist: Assign P01–P11 to the principal, GIS contractor, electrical contractor, and transaction counsel; document exactly which two seats enter at Scaled volume.

chapters.title: The First 30-Day Launch Sprint & Kill / Fix / Scale Gates
chapters.subtitle: A Four-Person Launch Pod for Utility-Validated MW, Separate BESS and AI Campus Options, Controlled Fee Burn, and Day-30/60/90 Capital Decisions
chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #47 ranks #15 of 49 with a 92/100 Money-to-Manpower Score. This sprint sequences 11 mapped plays into a four-person origination pod: one full-time principal and three contractors covering GIS, electrical diligence, and property rights. Days 1–7 establish buyer specifications and screen parcels; Days 8–14 test utility and zoning feasibility; Days 15–21 negotiate contingent options; Days 22–30 package evidence and make capital decisions. Separate 5–25-acre standalone BESS sites from fiber-, water-, and zoning-constrained AI campuses. Cap first-month cash deployment at $7,500 against a $25,000 launch account. Annual owner-profit cases remain $33,000 Conservative, $212,100 Base, and $486,000 Scaled. Day-30/60/90 thresholds expand diligence only when documented utility progress, buyer engagement, and remaining cash justify it.

sections.heading: 1. Days 1–7: Translate Eleven Plays into a Funded, Four-Person Search
paragraphs: Launch a narrow search rather than a speculative land portfolio. Candidate #47 has eleven mapped operator plays; use the following execution labels to connect them to observable work products. P01 captures developer requirements; P02 screens 69kV–345kV substations and corridors; P03 reconciles queue records; P04 identifies parcel owners; P05 checks floodplain, wetlands, mineral interests, and access; P06 verifies zoning pathways; P07 obtains utility service evidence; P08 verifies fiber and water; P09 structures assignable contingent options; P10 packages developer diligence; P11 negotiates assignment, milestone, and carry economics. These labels organize this chapter, rather than purporting to reproduce an external play taxonomy. Start with two adjacent jurisdictions and one utility territory. Select three credible developers whose written acquisition criteria cover either standalone storage or AI campuses. Record requested MW, acceptable service dates, acreage, security requirements, and upgrade budgets separately for each buyer. The principal owns outreach and investment decisions; a GIS contractor owns screening; an electrical contractor owns utility questions; a property-rights contractor owns title and option coordination. Retain appropriately licensed counsel or brokerage expertise within that third workstream. No contractor may promise capacity, sign an option, or authorize additional spending.

Fund the illustrative sprint with $25,000, inside the canonical $10,000–$50,000 startup range, and cap first-month cash deployment at $7,500. Allocate $4,500 to operating expense: $1,200 GIS support, $1,500 electrical support, $1,200 property-rights support, and $600 for software, records, and communications. Allocate another $1,000 to targeted external diligence and $2,000 to option consideration, leaving $17,500 untouched. The principal takes no cash draw during this sprint; personal living costs require separate funding. These are procurement ceilings, not assertions that specialist work fits every local market. Obtain fixed-scope quotes before ordering, and reduce parcel volume if quotes exceed the envelope. Reserve the entire $2,000 option allocation as potentially unrecoverable because utility or zoning diligence can eliminate otherwise attractive sites. This loss allowance describes the same cash, not another expense added twice. No study deposit, extension payment, or nonrefundable reservation may sit outside the ledger. Maintain weekly committed, paid, refundable, and remaining balances. A $10,000-funded launch must use a smaller screening-only scope until additional funding or developer-paid diligence becomes available; it cannot responsibly copy this $25,000 cash plan.

Build one evidence register in SQLite or a controlled spreadsheet, with QGIS handling spatial overlays. Every parcel record needs its assessor identifier, owner source, acreage, utility territory, nearest relevant facilities, source date, and separate confidence fields for physical observations and utility conclusions. Import public PJM queue material where applicable, FEMA flood layers, USFWS wetland screening layers, county zoning maps, and recorded property instruments. Public layers identify questions; they do not establish service availability, jurisdictional wetland boundaries, or marketable title. Set a first-week funnel of forty raw parcels, twelve desk-screen survivors, and six owner contacts with verified contact provenance. Split the twelve survivors between the two asset types rather than pooling acreage or power assumptions. Storage candidates must fit a 5–25-acre usable footprint with access, setbacks, and a plausible interconnection pathway. Campus candidates require buyer-specific expandable area, cooling strategy, fiber access, and a credible load-service pathway. Put proximity measurements in a geography field, never a deliverable-MW field. At the end of Day 7, the principal signs the source register and rejects records that cannot be reproduced from dated evidence.

callout.title: Buy Evidence Before Buying More Option Time
callout.body: Experienced originators protect bargaining leverage by resolving the most expensive uncertainties before increasing nonrefundable consideration.
items: Ask the utility which specific service study, tariff process, and customer authorization apply before purchasing an elaborate electrical concept package.
Request separate BESS charging and export assumptions; export feasibility does not establish import service or acceptable operating restrictions.
Ask fiber providers for route-level feasibility, construction responsibility, and diversity evidence; two carriers can share the same vulnerable conduit.
Negotiate diligence extensions against identifiable utility or planning events, with capped payments and written notice mechanics instead of automatic monthly fee escalation.

sections.heading: 2. Days 8–14: Replace Apparent Headroom with Utility and Land-Use Evidence
paragraphs: The second week converts attractive map positions into explicit utility questions. P07 should produce a utility-authored response or a documented route to the required study, not an originator's estimate dressed as capacity. Ask for the proposed service point, voltage, import and export requirements, study prerequisites, upgrade responsibility, indicative timing, and treatment of competing requests. A queue entry establishes an application record, not available headroom. A hosting-capacity map may describe a different voltage class or operating condition from the proposed project. For storage, document charging load and discharging output separately, including restrictions that could undermine dispatch economics. For an AI campus, obtain the buyer's ramp schedule and critical service requirements before asking about firm supply. Use 18 CFR 35.28 to understand applicable transmission-provider interconnection obligations, while checking the actual tariff and jurisdiction; generator procedures do not automatically supply a campus load-service commitment. Maintain three evidence levels: inquiry submitted, preliminary utility response, and study-supported service parameters. Only the final category supports modeled deliverable MW, and even then quote the utility's conditions and remaining contractual dependencies alongside the number.

P05 and P06 run in parallel because electrical progress cannot repair unusable property rights or a prohibited land use. For a Virginia search, check local authority under Va. Code § 15.2-2280 and obtain the current ordinance, parcel district, use classification, application calendar, and any adopted moratorium. A staff conversation is a lead, not an entitlement. Record whether storage is treated as a utility facility, industrial use, or another local category, and identify setbacks, fire access, landscaping, noise, and equipment-height requirements. Examine the usable pad after constraints, not the assessor's gross acreage. Check mineral reservations, surface-use rights, easements, road access, and restrictions that could block foundations or utility corridors. Wetland screening under Clean Water Act Section 404, 33 U.S.C. § 1344, identifies potential permitting work; database absence does not resolve jurisdiction or authorize fill. Campus water diligence must specify cooling architecture, source, required volume, wastewater disposition, and provider response. Do not charge a standalone BESS parcel for a campus-scale water assumption, but do capture its actual fire-protection and emergency-response requirements. Each unresolved item gets a named resolver, price ceiling, and decision date.

By Day 14, classify six priority parcels against the actual developer briefs and reduce them to no more than four negotiation candidates. Use a downside residual rather than a headline price per nearby megawatt. Start with the developer's supported project value at the documented service date; subtract land consideration, remaining development spending, supported upgrade exposure, financing and delay costs, and the developer's required return. The resulting headroom limits an assignment fee; it is not itself booked revenue. Where utility-supported MW or upgrade responsibility is absent, leave capacity-derived valuation at zero and negotiate only inexpensive contingent control. Stress the buyer model using a twelve-month service delay and a fifty-percent increase in the currently supported upgrade estimate. These are internal stress assumptions, not predictions of utility outcomes. Obtain buyer confirmation that the stressed residual still supports the proposed fee before increasing consideration. If no usable upgrade estimate exists, the stress test remains incomplete and the site cannot pass the capital-expansion test. Send developers an evidence summary that distinguishes observed facts, utility conditions, operator assumptions, and questions still awaiting third-party resolution.

callout.title: Four Verifications Before Any Nonrefundable Site Payment
callout.body: The principal signs these checks for each parcel; failure pauses payment even when the broader sprint remains on schedule.
items: Verify the option grantor's authority, the exact legal description, and the access rights needed to conduct the proposed diligence.
Verify the utility evidence label, keeping preliminary discussion separate from study-supported MW, cost allocation, and energization conditions.

sections.heading: 3. Days 15–21: Purchase Conditional Control and Build an Assignable Evidence Pack
paragraphs: P09 aims for two executed, diligence-contingent options, not maximum acreage under expensive paper. Seek twelve to twenty-four months of contractual control, with negotiated termination rights tied to utility feasibility, zoning, title, access, and buyer-defined physical requirements. That duration is a target, not an assumption that owners will accept cheap long-term exclusivity. If an owner requires consideration beyond the sprint allocation, negotiate staged extensions, obtain developer funding, or stop. Specify permitted assignees, assignment notice, any owner consent, diligence access, cooperation with utility requests, and treatment of studies after termination. Have counsel determine whether recording a memorandum is appropriate and authorized; avoid publishing commercial terms unnecessarily. Validate the principal-trading structure against applicable state licensing rules. Va. Code § 54.1-2100 defines broker activity, while § 54.1-2103 addresses specified exemptions; neither should be reduced to a universal claim that calling compensation an assignment fee eliminates licensing requirements. Where the activity requires brokerage licensure, use a properly licensed participant under a documented arrangement. Never market another owner's parcel as though the pod already controls it. Log execution, effective dates, payment receipts, and every termination notice deadline.

Keep the workload inside the one-FT-plus-three-contractor pod by enforcing work-in-process limits. The principal handles at most four active owner negotiations and three substantive developer conversations per week. The electrical contractor carries no more than six live utility inquiries; the GIS contractor updates only the twelve survivors; the property-rights contractor prepares no more than two executable option packages during this sprint. Batch factual questions daily and hold one thirty-minute exception meeting twice weekly. Automated reminders can track utility response dates, owner commitments, and option notices, but do not automate interpretations of capacity or legal rights. P10 should produce a versioned evidence pack containing the legal description, control instrument, rights exceptions, constraint map, zoning pathway, utility correspondence, study status, buyer infrastructure requirements, and financial assumptions. Redact personal contact details and share proprietary studies only with appropriate rights and recipient restrictions. Maintain a change log identifying what changed, its source, and which prior claims became stale. If a restudy or municipal action changes feasibility, withdraw the affected pricing sheet immediately and notify every developer who received it before negotiating further.

P11 separates executable economics from attractive but unearned deal value. An option assignment earns operator revenue only under the applicable contract and accounting treatment; a per-MW milestone must identify the verified capacity basis, triggering event, payer, and payment date. Development carry remains outside realized revenue until the relevant entitlement and recognition conditions are satisfied. Do not count land purchase price, battery procurement, campus construction spending, customer electricity purchases, or underlying project value as origination revenue. Review principal-versus-agent presentation under ASC 606 if the operator collects money on another party's behalf; pass-through collections do not become operator revenue simply by crossing its bank account. For each proposed transaction, maintain separate columns for contract face amount, recognition status, cash received, third-party obligations, and remaining collection risk. Give buyers an itemized transfer schedule rather than a single opaque premium. Where future upgrade costs remain unresolved, use conditional pricing or buyer-funded study milestones instead of manufacturing certainty. The first thirty days should create defensible control and a collection pathway; the canonical two-to-six-month first-deal window makes a Day-30 cash receipt possible but unnecessary.
